Abstract: To solve the problems of response delay and poor adaptability existing in traditional dynamic optimization methods caused by the strong nonlinearity, time-varying characteristics and multiple uncertainties of distillation processes, this paper proposes an intelligent dynamic optimization method based on digital twins and deep learning. The high-fidelity synchronization is realized by establishing a digital twin that integrates mechanism and data. CNN-BiLSTM-Attention (Convolutional Neural Network-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory-Attention) model is designed to capture dynamic features, and then Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) method is employed to generate optimization strategies online. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional method, the proposed method not only decreases the integral of absolute error (IAE) of product purity control to 0.45, but also reduces the energy consumption per unit product of distillation process to 127.8 kW•h/kg. Especially, the recovery time is greatly improved compared with comparative method when dealing with untrained disturbances. The closed loop of perception, decision-making and optimization is realized by this framework, which enhances the dynamic performance, economy and robustness of distillation process.  © 2026 The Authors.

Abstract: Accurate real-time estimation of electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption is essential for range prediction, energy management, and the development of digital twins for advanced mobility applications. However, existing driving simulators often rely on simplified vehicle models that fail to capture the interaction between driver behavior, vehicle dynamics, and battery-state evolution under realistic operating conditions. This paper presents a high-fidelity digital twin framework for real-time EV energy consumption estimation based on the co-simulation of a Unity driving environment and a physics-based battery model developed in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed architecture combines immersive vehicle dynamics, detailed road and terrain reconstruction, and a second-order equivalent circuit battery model through a low-latency User Datagram Protocol (UDP) communication layer, enabling synchronized real-time execution. The framework was calibrated using a Tesla Model 3 Standard Range and validated against experimental measurements collected on three real-world routes characterized by different traffic and operating conditions. Model accuracy was assessed through the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R2). Experimental results demonstrate high predictive accuracy, with route-dependent MAPE values ranging from 2.63% to 5.40% and a maximum R2 of 0.859. Furthermore, the proposed digital twin accurately reproduces energy-consumption trends over a wide range of initial battery State of Charge (SoC) conditions, from 96% to 28%. The analysis of residual errors highlights the influence of terrain elevation uncertainty, thermal effects of battery, and auxiliary loads on prediction accuracy. The results obtained demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a reliable and computationally efficient tool for EV energy assessment, digital-twin applications, eco-driving studies, and future intelligent charging and energy-management strategies. © 2013 IEEE.

Abstract: A digital twin is a virtual model that interacts bidirectionally with physical systems through closed-loop optimization. It has wide applications in aerospace, construction, and healthcare. Verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification of predictive models help ensure robust decisions and reliable outputs. Based on the previously developed conformal prediction method, mapped-dual adaptive conformal prediction (M-DACP) is proposed as extension, targeting application scenarios where multidimensional outputs jointly participate in decision-making. It enhances the ability to handle complex conditions such as non-exchangeable data and distribution shifts, especially when input information is limited. Using Apnea-ECG database, the reliability numerical analysis results and the diversity of result format, referable information provided by optimal transport (OT) are demonstrated, offering directions for future research.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Operational quality in sustainable buildings is often compromised by fragmentation across Building Information Modeling (BIM), the Internet of Things (IoT), and Building Management Systems (BMS). This paper proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-integrated Semantic Digital Twin (SDT) framework that redefines quality management as a traceable and governance-ready operational process. The framework combines ontology-driven semantics, hybrid physics-AI modeling, and a requirements-to-KPI traceability graph to connect lifecycle intent, data provenance, analytic outputs, and operator decisions. A seven-layer architecture is introduced together with an assurance loop that validates data, quantifies uncertainty, records explainability artifacts, and enforces human approval before controlled actuation. To address evaluation needs, the paper also defines a benchmark-ready Design Science Research blueprint using BOPTEST and governance metrics, including energy use intensity, comfort violation hours, CO2 exceedance hours, fault detection performance, uncertainty calibration, traceability completeness, and approval latency. The contribution is therefore not only an architectural model, but also a practical audit-ready basis for trustworthy and scalable building operations.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: AI-driven digital twin self-calibration and NC data optimization for improving form accuracy under a cycle-time invariant constraint in five-axis CNC machining
Source title: International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Dankook University, Yongin, 16890, South Korea
Authors with affiliations: Kang J., Department of Mechanical Engineering, Dankook University, Yongin, 16890, South Korea; Kim D., Department of Mechanical Engineering, Dankook University, Yongin, 16890, South Korea; Jee S., Department of Mechanical Engineering, Dankook University, Yongin, 16890, South Korea
Abstract: Five-axis free-form machining requires high form accuracy and productivity simultaneously, yet digital twins deployed in industry often lose predictive accuracy when tool paths, workpieces, or controller settings change. This paper presents an AI-driven framework that performs ROI-guided digital twin self-calibration, uncertainty-aware composite risk mapping, and cycle-time invariant NC data optimization. A single dry-run execution is used solely as the calibration and optimization input, whereas the resulting NC patches are validated through representative finish-cut machining experiments rather than by dry-run reproduction alone. We calibrate a grey-box feed-drive model with nonlinear friction via hierarchical Bayesian inference, combining parametric corrections with a surface-parameterized Gaussian process residual that also quantifies predictive uncertainty. The calibrated posterior is propagated to construct a composite risk map that fuses predicted form error, predictive variance, and jerk-saturation proximity, from which vulnerable regions are automatically extracted. Guided by these regions, a constrained optimization redistributes feedrate to reduce risk while enforcing a cycle-time invariant (non-increasing, controller-reported) constraint and a global improvement condition, yielding vendor-neutral NC patches that modify only feedrate commands. Experiments include finish-cut machining of a turbine-blade mold cavity on a custom PC-based five-axis testbed, with supplementary dry-run tests on a commercial CNC. The ROI-guided calibration improves local prediction accuracy and risk-map reliability. The resulting vendor-neutral NC patch reduces peak and mean form errors by 65.2% (28.2 → 9.8 μm) and 25.6% (3.9 → 2.9 μm), respectively, improves surface quality, and keeps the controller-reported cycle-time essentially unchanged. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag London Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Physics-Informed Digital Twins in Computational Engineering: a PRISMA-ScR Review of Physics-Informed Learning, Neural Operators, Uncertainty Quantification, Real-Time Updating, and Deployment Readiness
Source title: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
Affiliations: Faculty of Industrial Engineering and Technology Management, HIT–Holon Institute of Technology, 52 Golomb St., Holon, 5810201, Israel
Authors with affiliations: Fridkin S., Faculty of Industrial Engineering and Technology Management, HIT–Holon Institute of Technology, 52 Golomb St., Holon, 5810201, Israel
Abstract: Physics-informed digital twins in computational engineering require more than a simulation model or a machine-learning surrogate. They connect a physical asset to a computational representation, learn from data, quantify uncertainty, update under sensor information, and support engineering decisions under explicit latency and credibility constraints. This scoping review synthesizes six research questions on physics-informed learning, neural operators, uncertainty quantification, data assimilation, application-domain maturity, and evidence-informed method selection. Seventy-nine database-identified scholarly reports inform the synthesis; the RQ-specific counts are 15, 14, 13, 26, 27, and 17, with overlap permitted across questions. Each headline claim is appraised through test-set construction, baseline adequacy, in- versus out-of-distribution evaluation, uncertainty and failure analysis, validation provenance, and complete sensing-to-decision latency. Numerical errors, speedups, and update times are interpreted within their study-specific evaluation settings rather than as universal selection thresholds. The evidence indicates that physics-informed neural networks can support bounded inverse, surrogate, and sparse-data tasks, but their maturity is constrained by optimization pathologies, boundary enforcement, numerical baselines, and distribution shift. Neural operators provide moderate evidence of acceleration for repeated partial differential equation prediction, but only limited evidence as complete digital-twin backbones because offline cost, geometry and regime transfer, uncertainty calibration, and operational synchronization are inconsistently reported. Uncertainty quantification and data assimilation are essential credibility and synchronization layers, yet calibration non-identifiability, misuse of information-based covariance bounds, ensemble miscalibration, filter divergence, observability limits, and incomplete end-to-end validation remain common. A non-compensatory evidence-gate procedure converts the critical synthesis into method-selection guidance while preserving negative, conflicting, and unreported evidence. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Safety-Constrained Multimodal Digital Twins for Zero-Defect Industrial Workcells
Source title: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Technologies, CONIT 2026
Affiliations: Amazon, United States; Amazon, United States
Authors with affiliations: Sharma A., Amazon, United States; Mallala N., Amazon, United States
Abstract: Zero-defect operation in industrial workcells depends on catching process drift early enough to act before defects propagate, but many deployed digital twins still function mainly as monitoring tools. This paper presents an Agentic Multimodal Digital Twin (AMDT) that combines synchronized telemetry, vision, event logs, and process context with calibrated defect-risk prediction and an uncertainty-aware intervention policy. The system makes a concrete set of design choices: gated cross-attention fusion with signal-quality weighting, Monte Carlo dropout for epistemic uncertainty estimation (T = 20 forward passes), and a bounded action layer whose thresholds are calibrated on held-out data. We evaluate the approach in two scenarios, an automated fastening cell and an item-sortation line. In those settings, the AMDT reaches lead times of 4.1 cycles and 7.8 items, compared with 2.8 cycles and 5.1 items for the best single-modality baselines, reduces unnecessary autonomous interventions by 38-40% through uncertainty gating, and maintains at least 97% throughput retention. Ablation results show that different modalities matter for different defect mechanisms. Overall, the results show how a digital twin can be extended from passive monitoring to bounded, safety-constrained intervention in a setting. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Trust Beyond Perfection: Managing Uncertainty in the Internet of Digital Twins
Source title: IEEE International Conference on Communications
Affiliations: University of Cagliari, DIEE, Cagliari, Italy
Authors with affiliations: Marche C., University of Cagliari, DIEE, Cagliari, Italy; Piras L.L., University of Cagliari, DIEE, Cagliari, Italy; Nitti M., University of Cagliari, DIEE, Cagliari, Italy
Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly adopted in IoT systems as autonomous agents capable of providing services and interacting within distributed ecosystems. However, most trust management solutions rely on overly idealized assumptions: service evaluations are always accurate, and benevolent nodes never make mistakes. These assumptions limit the applicability of such models in realistic scenarios, where uncertainty and imperfection are the norm. This paper proposes a trust management model tailored to more realistic DTs, where both service providers and requesters may introduce errors. Providers may fail due to physical or software limitations; requesters cannot rely on objective ground truth to evaluate outcomes. To capture this complexity, we introduce a feedback mechanism based on divergence from aggregated results, rather than binary correctness. We define an IoT scenario where DTs dynamically offer and request services. A trust computation model is applied to distinguish truly malicious nodes from those affected by faults, reducing false positives. Simulations confirm improved trust accuracy and system resilience under realistic conditions. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Assessing the impact of AI-enabled BIM digital twins on construction risks: a Bayesian Network of Jordanian expert beliefs
Source title: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
Affiliations: Faculty of Engineering, Civil Department, Jadara University, Irbid, Jordan; Faculty of Engineering Technology, Zarqa University, Zarqa, Jordan; Faculty of Engineering, Isra University, Amman, Jordan
Authors with affiliations: Albtoush F., Faculty of Engineering, Civil Department, Jadara University, Irbid, Jordan; Al-Btoosh J.A.A., Faculty of Engineering Technology, Zarqa University, Zarqa, Jordan; Rawashdeh T.M., Faculty of Engineering, Isra University, Amman, Jordan; Al-Btoush M.A.K.A., Faculty of Engineering, Isra University, Amman, Jordan
Abstract: Building projects in Jordan routinely experience substantial schedule delays and cost overruns, yet robust empirical evidence on the impacts of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Building Information Modelling (BIM)-based Digital Twins remains scarce. This study develops a belief-based, probabilistic causal model of how AI-enabled BIM Digital Twin technologies may affect time–cost risks in Jordanian reinforced-concrete building projects. Using structured expert elicitation with 600 experienced practitioners (contractors, consultants, project managers, and academics), we capture expert judgements on causal links between four technology clusters—AI-based progress detection, contract-aware BIM assistants, predictive cost–schedule twins, and AI-assisted design/constructability—and key project mechanisms and outcomes. All quantitative results in this study come from these expert judgements; no project-level before–after performance data are used. Accordingly, results are reported as pooled expert beliefs under stated scenarios, not empirically validated predictions. Hierarchical Bayesian models pool elicited probabilities into a Bayesian Network (BN) representing collective expert beliefs, rather than observed project performance. Monte Carlo simulations, Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA), and Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI) are then used to explore technology-adoption and policy scenarios and to rank influential levers. Experts believe that, under idealized, high-readiness conditions, AI-enabled BIM Digital Twins could sharply reduce the probabilities of schedule delays >20% and cost overruns >10%. These figures are belief-based, optimistic upper-bound expectations derived from expert judgement, not empirically measured or validated impacts. The Bayesian Network therefore serves as an uncertainty-aware decision-support tool for early policy and investment decisions in data-poor contexts. It highlights the roles of training, organizational readiness, and client demand alongside technology adoption. Copyright © 2026 Albtoush, Al-Btoosh, Rawashdeh and Al-Btoush.

Abstract: A probabilistic digital twin framework is developed for fatigue prognosis of aerospace structures by fusing passive sensing based on higher harmonic analysis, historical test data, and physics-based crack-growth models within a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN). Three progressive data assimilation schemes are evaluated: (i) purely online sensing, (ii) hybrid transition from historical-to-online data, and (iii) conditional progressive fusion of both sources. Transfer learning leverages offline experiments to constrain priors, enabling rapid convergence of material parameter posteriors and effective initial flaw size estimation while reducing the volume of online observations. Experimental validation on a metallic plate with a central hole under constant-amplitude cyclic loading demonstrates accurate whole-life prognosis, with DBN predictions closely tracking observed crack evolution while quantifying measurement, material, and model uncertainties via calibrated credible intervals. Benchmarking against Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) highlights the DBN’s superior sequential uncertainty quantification, while GPR offers computational efficiency for near-real-time extrapolation. The hybrid DBN framework thus provides robust, uncertainty-aware life prognosis, advancing digital twin methodologies for aerospace applications. Copyright © 2025. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Abstract: The integration of Digital Twins (DTs) into healthcare promises transformative advancements in personalized medicine, resource optimization, and predictive analytics. However, ethical concerns about data privacy, algorithmic bias, and accountability remain critical barriers to widespread adoption. This study combines quantitative and qualitative analyses (n = 120 participants) to explore public perception and ethical implications of DTs in healthcare. Results reveal a significant correlation between prior knowledge of DTs and positive perception (78% vs. 52% among uninformed respondents, p = 0.012), with data security (45%) and regulatory uncertainty (32%) emerging as primary concerns. Qualitative insights highlight demands for transparent governance frameworks and patient-centric safeguards. The discussion underscores the dual potential of DTs: enabling precision medicine through wearable sensors and predictive modeling, while risking systemic inequities if deployed without rigorous oversight. We argue that proactive regulation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and public education are essential to balance innovation with ethical responsibility. This work contributes a roadmap for integrating DTs into healthcare, emphasizing the need for adaptive policies and clinical validation to ensure equitable and sustainable implementation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: Digital twins couple computational models with physical systems to enable services such as predictive reasoning and runtime analysis that support decision–making for maintenance, optimisation and system evolution. They create a technically rich setting for applying formal methods throughout the system lifecycle beyond design-time. This tutorial introduces the elements of digital twin technology, identifying emerging opportunities for formal techniques, including the verification of evolving models under uncertainty, integration of heterogeneous models and rigorous composition of digital twin-enabled systems. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Uncertainty-Aware 3D Generative Scene Completion for Industrial Digital Twin Initialization under Occlusion
Source title: IISE Annual Conference and Expo 2026
Affiliations: Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States
Authors with affiliations: Woo S., Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States; Woo S.H., Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States; Son Y.-J., Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States
Abstract: Digital twin (DT) environment model initialization and updates are increasingly essential for manufacturing commissioning, reconfiguration, and robot planning, yet accurate 3D DT creation remains a major bottleneck: current practice often requires months of manual CAD modeling, delaying ramp-up after new installations or layout changes. Although autonomous mobile robots can scan facilities rapidly, industrial scenes exhibit severe occlusions and sensing gaps, which makes DT initialization under partial observability unreliable when missing structure is completed deterministically without representing uncertainty. We propose a confidence-guided, uncertainty-aware hierarchical scene completion framework that accelerates DT initialization while explicitly quantifying the unknown. First, we derive a per-voxel confidence signal from truncated signed distance fields (TSDF) fusion statistics (integration weights) and partition the map into local blocks. Unlike prior completion pipelines that uniformly hallucinate missing regions, we select only structurally uncertain blocks for generative inference and preserve well-observed regions unchanged. This design improves computational efficiency and prevents overwriting trusted geometry. Second, we develop a 3-level hierarchical Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for volumetric completion with multi-scale latent variables and a dual-head encoder-decoder that jointly predicts TSDF geometry and semantic labels. The probabilistic formulation yields calibrated per-voxel uncertainty via latent sampling and uncertainty propagation across scales. Experiments on the ScanNet dataset under 60% sparsity reveal that our method achieves 73.6% occupied Intersection over Union (IoU) and 85.5% semantic mean IoU, while substantially improving performance in truly unobserved space (74.5% IoU on unobserved voxels versus 9.11% for a deterministic method). Overall, our selective probabilistic completion provides competitive reconstruction quality and practical uncertainty estimates for rapid DT deployment in occluded industrial environments. © (2026) by Institute of Industrial & Systems Engineers (IISE) All rights reserved.

Abstract: The development of a Digital Twin (DT) for spacecraft represents a key step in the digital transformation of space systems, which has the potential to enable high fidelity simulation capabilities, enhanced mission situational awareness, procedure validation, autonomous operations and predictive maintenance, to mention a few. A DT relies on simulation models with configurable parameters that must be calibrated to accurately represent the behaviour of the real system. Commonly used approaches for the calibration of spacecraft simulation models are optimization-based methods, such as numerical techniques and evolutionary algorithms. However, they do not incorporate uncertainty quantification (UQ), which is a fundamental requirement for the development of accurate and reliable twinning technologies. In this light, we propose a Bayesian calibration framework that accounts for various sources of uncertainty, including model parameter uncertainty, model form uncertainty, and observation uncertainty. It provides posterior estimates for model parameters and credible intervals for model predictions. Also, the framework is applied to the real data of European Space Agency (ESA)’s Cluster mission to calibrate a predictive model for solar array degradation and power generation. The results indicate that the proposed approach provides robust model calibration under uncertainty and effectively reduces model discrepancy, showing significant improvements over previous approaches. © 2025 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Overcoming Uncertainty With an Ensemble of Physical Models and Real-Time Measurements: Thermal Error Compensation Using Kalman Filters In a Digital Twin
Source title: Lecture Notes in Production Engineering
Affiliations: Advanced Manufacturing Laboratory, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland; inspire AG, Zurich, Switzerland
Authors with affiliations: Lang S., Advanced Manufacturing Laboratory, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland, inspire AG, Zurich, Switzerland; Schneider M., Advanced Manufacturing Laboratory, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland; Rhiner L., Advanced Manufacturing Laboratory, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland, inspire AG, Zurich, Switzerland; Bambach M., Advanced Manufacturing Laboratory, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland
Abstract: Thermally induced errors critically limit precision in machine tools (MT), affecting dimensional accuracy in high-precision manufacturing. Physics-based models offer a sustainable solution and can do without training measurements, unlike data-driven models, but are often unsuitable for real-time thermal error compensation due to computational demands and boundary condition uncertainties. This paper presents an enhanced ensemble Kalman filter approach to accurately and efficiently reconstruct the thermal state from limited sensor data. Utilizing a reduced finite element model generated via Krylov modal subspace techniques, the proposed method integrates real-time sensor measurements with an ensemble of perturbed models to robustly estimate thermal states and mechanical deformations. Validation experiments on a thermal test bench with 10 out of 40 temperature sensors observed demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy achieving an RMSE of 1.5∘C. The computational speed is over 45× faster than real-time allowing the implementation of the digital twin for any MT. The reduction of the volumetric thermal error by consistently more than 70% confirm the potential of this digital twin-based approach for real-time thermal error compensation in precision manufacturing. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Bio360: A Multimodal Framework for Health Digital Twin Modeling and Early Physiological Drift Detection

Affiliations: Clarksburg High School, Clarksburg, MD, United States; Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, United States; Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology, Department of Ece, Bangalore, India

Abstract: Continuous physiological monitoring through wearable devices and digital health applications has become increasingly prevalent; however, clinically meaningful interpretation of these signals remains limited due to fragmented data ecosystems, heterogeneous sampling characteristics, and reliance on isolated threshold-based alerts. This paper presents Bio360, a multimodal Health Digital Twin (HDT) framework designed to integrate wearable biosignals, health and fitness applications, nutrition and lifestyle inputs, and longitudinal clinical data into a unified, continuously evolving digital health representation. The framework emphasizes longitudinal analysis, personalized baseline-relative interpretation, and contextual multisignal convergence rather than isolated physiological measurements. Bio360 incorporates a four-pillar multimodal architecture supported by a harmonization and normalization pipeline capable of integrating heterogeneous physiological streams across wearable platforms with differing temporal resolutions, signal fidelity, and device-specific schemas. The system further introduces a Contextual Event Evaluator (CEE) that aggregates baseline-relative deviations, signal weighting, and trend persistence into a composite Event Confidence Score (ECS) for identifying potentially meaningful physiological drift. To strengthen predictive interpretation under uncertainty, the framework incorporates Bayesian probabilistic modeling that continuously updates confidence estimates as new physiological and contextual data become available. A representative cardiovascular monitoring scenario demonstrates how persistent convergence among elevated resting heart rate, reduced heart rate variability, altered sleep architecture, behavioral stress patterns, laboratory biomarkers, and family history may collectively indicate emerging physiological risk despite individually nominal measurements. Bio360 further extends beyond physiological modeling through the introduction of a Behavioral Digital Twin (BDT), which incorporates adherence, behavioral routines, and wellness engagement into the broader digital twin ecosystem. The proposed framework aims to support early physiological drift detection, simulation-driven predictive health modeling, and scalable longitudinal health intelligence for future preventive healthcare systems. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This study developed a digital twin (DT)-driven framework for real-time fatigue crack detection and prediction in steel structures based on computer vision and fracture mechanics. A steel crack detection method was proposed to extract actual crack data from inspection images based on the developed DeepLabV3+ model. A machine learning-assisted probabilistic fatigue crack growth (PFCG) model was established to accelerate the generation of the virtual crack data. On this basis, a DT-driven framework was established by integrating computer vision-based surface crack length information and the PFCG model to reduce the uncertainties. The parameter uncertainties in the PFCG model were quantified by Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs). Experimental studies were conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed DT-driven framework. The results show that the fatigue crack detections and predictions are in good agreement with experimental results. The proposed DT-driven framework has a particularly pronounced improvement in lightweight steel crack detection, and can effectively update the model parameters to accurately predict the fatigue life of steel structures. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A Spatio-Temporal Diffusion Approach for Communication-Efficient Digital Twin Synchronization

Abstract: Digital twin (DT) provides an effective paradigm for modeling and monitoring large-scale spatio-temporal traffic sensing systems by constructing real-time virtual replicas of geographically distributed roadside sensing entities. However, practical deployment of DT is challenged by the excessive uplink communication overhead incurred by continuous real-time state synchronization. To fill this gap, we propose a communication-efficient DT synchronization framework that combines selective uplink reporting at the base station with diffusion-based state completion at the DT server. Leveraging the uncertainty estimation capability of diffusion models, we quantify reconstruction uncertainty by measuring the variability of spatio-temporal states across multiple diffusion-based completion samples, and jointly incorporate node importance derived from the underlying geographic connectivity to capture spatial redundancy. Numerical results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms random masking in DT reconstruction accuracy under the same communication budget, demonstrating its effectiveness for communication-efficient DT synchronization. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors with affiliations: Prakash N.B., Qis College of Engineering & Technology, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Ongole, India; Senthil M., Qis College of Engineering & Technology, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Ongole, India; Srinu N., Qis College of Engineering & Technology, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Ongole, India
Abstract: Accurate prediction of emergency material demand after earthquakes is essential for effective disaster response following earthquakes is vital to disaster preparedness and relief activities; however, such forecasting can be difficult owing to lack of data, dynamic environment, and high uncertainties involved. Conventional models which depend on past experiences, along with static machine learning techniques, cannot adapt to changing situations and lack causal relationships. In this work, a new method called Causal Digital Twin-Driven Emergency Material Demand Prediction (CDT-EMDP) has been developed that incorporates causal reasoning, digital twin simulations, agent-based analysis, and Bayesian modeling to address the challenge. CDT-EMDP builds a causal graph showing the relationship between seismogenic intensity, damage, and human displacement. The simulation of a disaster scenario is conducted via digital twin, and the agent-based simulation predicts emergency material demands in an adaptive manner. Real-time feedback is used to refine predictions according to newly acquired data. The experiments conducted on the proposed method using simulated earthquake scenarios reveal that the model performs with an accuracy of 92.8%, outperforming traditional methods. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The pharmaceutical industry is increasingly adopting artificial intelligence(AI)-driven modeling frameworks to address rising system complexity, stringent regulatory expectations, and the demand for robust, efficient manufacturing processes. AI-driven digital twins have emerged as a central enabling technology in this context, providing continuously updated virtual representations of pharmaceutical processes and products that integrate mechanistic understanding with data-driven learning. This review examines the role of AI-driven digital twins in model-informed pharmaceutical manufacturing and quality systems, with an emphasis on hybrid mechanistic and machine-learning (ML) architectures, real-time model updating, and predictive process control. It discusses how these systems support quality by design, continuous manufacturing, and real-time release testing by enabling enhanced process understanding, deviation prediction, and lifecycle optimization beyond traditional static models. Particular attention is given to model validation, credibility assessment, uncertainty quantification, and regulatory acceptance, which are critical for the deployment of AI-driven digital twins in regulated pharmaceutical environments. By synthesizing current methodologies, regulatory perspectives, and emerging industrial applications, this article positions AI-driven digital twins as a foundational technology for next-generation pharmaceutical manufacturing and regulatory decision-making. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Graph Neural Network-Based Digital Twin Framework for Predictive Maintenance of Robotic Manipulators

Abstract: The growing integration of digital twin (DT) technology and predictive maintenance (PdM) has improved fault management in robotic manipulators, yet most existing methods still rely on sequential deep learning models that overlook mechanical dependencies and lack interpretability. Conventional approaches such as CNN, LSTM, and Transformer primarily focus on temporal signal trends, resulting in limited robustness to sensor noise and dynamic operating conditions. To address these gaps, this study proposes a Graph Neural Network-based Digital Twin Predictive Maintenance (GNN-DT-PM) framework that represents the manipulator as a spatio-temporal graph, where nodes denote sensorized joints and edges capture torque, vibration, and thermal correlations. A dual-stream GNN encoder fuses real-world telemetry with digital twin simulations, while an uncertainty-aware attention mechanism dynamically adjusts node contributions based on prediction confidence. A secure aggregation module further ensures data privacy and communication efficiency. Experimental results on a 6-DOF manipulator dataset show that GNN-DT-PM achieves 10.88% higher fault-prediction accuracy, 11.2% lower RMSE, and 16.22% faster inference latency than state-of-the-art baselines. Moreover, interpretability analysis confirms that the model's attention maps align with physical fault locations, enhancing diagnostic transparency. These findings demonstrate that GNN-DT-PM provides a practical, interpretable, and reproducible framework for reliable predictive maintenance in robotic systems. © The Institution of Engineering & Technology 2025.

Title: From Associational to Causality-Aware Digital Twins: An Architectural Framework
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Affiliations: RWTH University Hospital, Aachen, Germany; Department of Computer Science, RWTH Aachen University, Aachen, Germany
Authors with affiliations: Raju T.B., RWTH University Hospital, Aachen, Germany; Laevens B.P.M., RWTH University Hospital, Aachen, Germany; Meeßen C., RWTH University Hospital, Aachen, Germany; Schneider C.V., RWTH University Hospital, Aachen, Germany; Geisler S., Department of Computer Science, RWTH Aachen University, Aachen, Germany
Abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and the growing availability of large-scale data have led to the integration of predictive models within digital twin (DT) architectures. However, most existing DT architectures remain primarily associational, limiting their ability to incorporate domain knowledge, address uncertainty, and reason about the effects of interventions. Moreover, explainability in current AI-enabled DTs is often post-hoc rather than structurally embedded. In safety-critical domains like healthcare, these limitations reduce the transparency and reliability of DTs. Hence, we propose the concept of an architecture for data-driven, causality-aware DTs that integrates the causal model layer and a causal inference engine within DT frameworks. The proposed architecture allows for evaluating the influence of different interventions on the system, causal reasoning, and uncertainty-aware decision support while integrating domain knowledge into the twins’ representations. By moving from predictive modeling to causally grounded DTs, the framework enhances the interpretability of model outcomes and supports reliable decision-making. The paper aims to contribute to the foundation for next-generation DTs capable of moving beyond correlation-based intelligence toward causally aware and trustworthy systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: Aiming at the key challenges of source-load uncertainty, complexity of multi-energy coupling, and insufficient load-side regulation potential faced by multi-energy virtual power plant (MEVPP) in the operation process, this paper proposes a distributed model predictive control strategy based on digital twins. First, a dynamic digital twin resource aggregation model is constructed by combining deep neural network and improved k-means spectral clustering technique, which effectively realizes the dynamic aggregation modeling and uncertainty portrayal of distributed renewable energy sources; second, in order to fully tap the regulation potential of the load-side, a charging and discharging pricing strategy based on real-time tariffs and incentive mechanisms is proposed, and a stepwise dynamic carbon trading scheme is introduced; and lastly. Finally, a digital twin-driven state-space prediction model is established to map the real-time state of the physical system into the digital space, provide a high-fidelity digital basis for distributed model predictive control (DMPC), and adopt the hierarchical coordination strategy of “day-ahead planning - intra-day rolling - real-time adjustment” to realize the dynamic optimization and control of the multi-energy virtual power plant. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy can effectively cope with the uncertainty and complexity of the multi-energy system, significantly improve the economy and stability of the virtual power plant operation, and provide technical support for the intelligent operation of the virtual power plant under the new type of power system. © (2026), (Power System Technology Press). Title: Integration of AI-driven digital twins for real-time optimization of renewable energy grids

Affiliations: Department of Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Kampala, Uganda
Authors with affiliations: Nneoma Ugwu C., Department of Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Kampala, Uganda; Chukwudi Ogenyi F., Department of Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Kampala, Uganda; Nnenna Ugwu J., Department of Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Kampala, Uganda; Okechukwu Ugwu P.-C., Department of Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Kampala, Uganda; Ben Okon M., Department of Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Kampala, Uganda
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar photovoltaics, wind turbines, hydropower, and energy storage systems, introduces substantial variability and complexity into modern power grids. This variability challenges grid stability, supply-demand balancing, and operational resilience. Digital twin (DT) technology, which provides a dynamic, real-time virtual representation of physical assets and systems, has emerged as a transformative tool for monitoring, analyzing, and optimizing energy grids. The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into digital twins further enhances their capabilities, enabling predictive analytics, adaptive control, fault detection, and real-time decision-making for grid-specific objectives such as voltage/frequency regulation, congestion management, DER coordination, curtailment reduction, and resilience under fast renewable ramps. Machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning techniques facilitate accurate forecasting of energy generation and demand, intelligent dispatch of distributed energy resources, and predictive maintenance, while hybrid models combining physics-based simulations with AI improve prediction accuracy in data-sparse or high-uncertainty environments. Despite these advancements, challenges persist, including data quality and availability, computational scalability, cybersecurity risks, and interoperability issues. This review synthesizes current research on AI-driven digital twins in renewable energy grids, highlights methodological and technological gaps, and identifies future research directions for developing resilient, scalable, and adaptive energy systems. The findings underscore the potential of AI-integrated digital twins to accelerate the transition toward intelligent, sustainable, and climate-resilient energy infrastructures. In addition, this review incorporates sustainability-oriented intelligent-system methodologies such as energy-aware edge–cloud cyber-physical architectures and digital-twin-enabled lifecycle sustainability frameworks to align DT optimization with contemporary sustainability practice better. Abstract: Power grid digital twins (DTs) face a fundamental challenge: uniformly modeling and maintaining consistency across time scales from microsecond-level electromagnetic transients to hour-level economic dispatch. Existing multi-rate simulation techniques have not been systematically integrated into DT frameworks, and current research lacks a theoretical definition for cross-scale consistency. This paper proposes a physics-informatics cross-domain consistency-driven method. A hierarchical multi-rate simulation architecture decomposes the grid DT into Electromagnetic Transient (EMT), electromechanical Transient (RMS), and quasi-steady-state layers. A cross-scale state synchronization algorithm with error propagation suppression is developed. A novel 'Layered Age-of-Information (LAoI)' and 'Twin Bias' framework quantifies uncertainty and consistency. Theoretical analysis establishes boundedness of error propagation, asymptotic stability of the multi-scale observer, contraction of uncertainty propagation, and LAoI thresholds derived from dominant time constants. This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for multi-time scale consistent DT modeling, including stability proofs, error bounds, and convergence guarantees. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Accurate battery state-of-health (SOH) estimation is essential for reliable electric vehicle operation. This paper presents a unified digital twin framework that combines attention-based sequence modeling with physics-guided learning for robust SOH prediction. Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for the context of integrating urban digital twins with the high-performance computing (HPC) to model, analyse, as well as accelerate pathways to city-wide carbon neutrality. Urban abstract simulations consist of digital twins of cities integrating heterogenous streams of data, physical models, and machine learning surrogates to simulate the behaviour and conditions of cities both spatially and temporally. HPC provides computational envelope capable of executing detailed building energy modelling, transport systems modelling, renewable generation modelling and coupled atmosphere-urban microclimate modelling both at city scale and at a temporal scale suitable to do sound policy analysis. The modular digital twin system comprises a system of interaction between building energy simulation and urban mobility models and distributed energy resource (DER) models and an urban carbon scoring engine. Its structure experiences HPC in order to compute a great number of scenarios in order to measure uncertainty and apply multi-objective analysis with the aim of minimizing emissions, costs and resilience. To explain the approach, a case study of synthetic city is conducted, and sensitivity experiments of electrification, deep retrofit, distributed photovoltaics, storage, and demand response portfolios is carried. Results quantify trade-offs between decarbonization rate, cost of energy, and stressors resilience and show that HPC-based digital twin's communities can be used to discover near-Pareto-optimal trade-offs in the presence of epistemic and aleatory uncertainty. The last point is on the implementation problems, data handlings and research plans to operationalize the city digital twins as a decision support system to simplify into carbon neutral city. © 2026, Dr. Yashwant Research Labs Pvt. Abstract: In the conditions of increasing complexity and uncertainty in urban logistics, digital twin technologies are considered a promising tool for improving the efficiency of transport and logistics systems. Despite the active development of digital twins in scientific research and engineering practice, empirical evidence on the readiness of urban logistics operators to adopt these technologies remains limited. The aim of this study is to assess the readiness of urban logistics operators to implement digital twin technologies based on a survey of managerial staff from logistics and courier companies. The empirical basis of the study is formed from a survey of 64 middle- and senior-level managers operating in seven major Russian cities. The study investigates the level of awareness of digital twin technologies, the digital and organizational readiness of companies, the expected operational and economic effects, as well as the main barriers to implementation. The results show that, despite a moderate level of managerial awareness, the expected benefits of digital twin adoption are assessed significantly higher than the current level of readiness and availability of internal competencies. Comparative and regression analyses confirm that the intention to launch pilot digital twin projects is primarily driven by the expected benefits, the level of awareness, and data readiness. The practical significance of the study lies in the potential use of the results for self-assessment of the digital maturity of logistics companies and for substantiating a phased approach to the implementation of digital twin technologies in urban logistics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: This paper proposes a formally grounded intelligent multi-agent Digital Twin framework for the modeling, monitoring, and coordinated management of catastrophic events in distributed cyber-physical environments. The proposed architecture integrates distributed sensing devices, real-time data assimilation, Digital Twin-based state estimation, predictive modeling, inter-agent communication, and hierarchical decision support within a closed-loop adaptive control structure. The dynamics of catastrophic processes are described through stochastic spatial-temporal models, while system-level coordination, synchronization, and concurrency are represented using timed Petri nets. In addition, a global stochastic optimal control formulation is introduced to minimize expected risk and intervention costs under uncertainty. To illustrate the applicability of the framework, a flood-monitoring scenario in the Dniester River Delta is considered, involving 20 Digital Twin devices and 4 cooperative decision-making agents. The resulting model provides a structured basis for distributed monitoring, risk assessment, scalable coordination, and adaptive response in real time. The proposed framework offers a rigorous formal and architectural foundation for future simulation, formal verification, experimental validation, and deployment-oriented implementations in resilient disaster-management systems.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Reliable and incentive-aware edge service provisioning is critical for emerging vehicular applications. Conventional edge scheduling and offloading methods mainly optimize instantaneous performance, often neglecting provider incentives and dynamic service uncertainty. Purely price-driven procurement similarly fails to capture key non-price factors in highly dynamic vehicular environments, such as mobility, interruption risk, and service continuity. We study a digital twin (DT)-enabled vehicular edge service market, comprising a platform acting as auctioneer, latency-sensitive mobile task requesters, and heterogeneous edge providers hosting standardized virtual service units. To enable responsive, trustworthy, and economically robust scheduling, we propose a digital-twin-guided online trust-aware reverse auction mechanism, termed Agora. Agora integrates DT-based quality evaluation with online reverse auctioning, jointly considering quoted asks and non-price attributes, including delay, interruption risk, continuity mismatch, trust level, and twinmaintenance overhead. A critical-payment rule ensures meaningful provider incentives while maintaining competitive welfare and service performance. Abstract: Supply chain disruptions caused by demand fluctuations and supply uncertainties pose significant challenges to traditional supply chain systems. Conventional decision-making approaches often rely on static information and lack real-time responsiveness, resulting in poor adaptability under sudden shocks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a supply chain resilience evaluation framework based on Digital Twin and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. A dynamic inventory model is constructed to simulate a three-echelon supply chain system under stochastic demand and disruption scenarios. Two operational modes, namely a traditional static policy and a digital twin-driven dynamic policy, are compared through discrete-time simulation. The results show that, compared with the traditional system, the digital twin-enabled approach reduces inventory fluctuation by approximately 45%-55%, decreases shortage levels by over 90%, and improves recovery speed by around 40% under disruption scenarios. These findings demonstrate that integrating real-time data and virtual simulation significantly enhances supply chain resilience by enabling proactive and adaptive decision-making. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent, severe, and complex driven by global warming and climate change, posing escalating threats to ecosystems, infrastructure, public health, and community safety worldwide. Recent advances in Earth observation, artificial intelligence, physics-based modelling, and cyberinfrastructure have accelerated the development of wildfire digital twins (WFDTs), yet existing capabilities remain fragmented across monitoring, fusion, prediction, simulation, and decision support. Unlike prior reviews that primarily address individual aspect of wildfire, this review and vision paper provides an integrated synthesis of WFDTs. We propose a six-layer WFDT architecture, identify six core capabilities spanning situational awareness through adaptive learning, and organise applications across the wildfire lifecycle from prevention and detection to response, smoke management, and post-fire recovery. Building upon these advances, we outline a research roadmap toward autonomous WFDTs through advances in hybrid intelligence, trustworthy AI, uncertainty quantification, decision intelligence, and continual learning. We envision that the defining characteristic of future WFDTs is not increasingly realistic digital representation, but their evolution into a new paradigm that continuously integrates sensing, prediction, uncertainty quantification, optimisation, governance, and human expertise towards a paradigm of intelligent, trustworthy decision infrastructures that continuously support human-centred wildfire decision making. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: Cardiac-valve repair is increasingly performed with minimal invasive approaches including robotic and catheter techniques that hinges on fragmented imaging modalities. Heart valve repair or replacement decisions are often made intraoperatively on the arrested heart, limiting the ability to assess the success of a repair prior to completing the surgery. It is difficult to monitor and predict intra-operative hemodynamic pressure on the arrested heart including device telemetry, which leaves the surgical team without a reliable, physics-based prediction of valve mechanics prior to the valve repair. Existing patient-specific simulations often run off-line; they omit closed-loop data assimilation, uncertainty policing, and regulatory-grade software controls. In this paper, we present a unified, intra-operative digital twin framework that closes the cyber-physical loop between the patient and surgical devices while conforming to ASME V&V-40, FDA modeling guidance, and IEC 62304 Class C software. The architecture integrates five elements: (i) a HL7/DICOM/IEEE 1588 data pipeline that harmonizes multimodal imaging, physiologic waveforms, robotic telemetry, and workflow video; (ii) a Bayesian assimilation engine that fuses these streams into a patient-specific latent state and covariance in real time; (iii) a GPU-accelerated, partitioned multi-physics core that couples reduced-order leaflet mechanics, immersed-boundary lattice Boltzmann hemodynamics, and lumped-parameter circulation via a predictor-corrector coupler; (iv) a generalized polynomial chaos ensemble that propagates both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty; and (v) a decision support platform that pairs an uncertainty-aware model predictive controller (MPC) with a reinforcement learning supervisor. They are embedded within a tiered human-in-the-loop authority arbiter. An implementation roadmap - (i) bench-top hardware-in-the-loop, (ii) pre-clinical translation, and (iii) regulatory submission - is outlined to guide deployment and validation.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Earthquakes pose severe threats to urban safety. Traditional prediction methods fail to fully quantify seismic uncertainties and address low-probability, high-impact 'long-tail risks'. This paper proposes a partially validated probabilistic urban seismic damage prediction framework integrating large-scale scenario ensembles and digital twins. The framework is conceptually designed with four layers: data fusion, digital twin modeling, scenario ensemble simulation, and probabilistic assessment. Due to current data and computational constraints, empirical validation is limited to two core modules - the PI-GAN ground motion generation module and the probabilistic damage cloud module - using the 2021 Yangbi Ms6.4 earthquake (single event, single region). The remaining two modules (infrastructure cascading failure and social behavior modeling) are presented as conceptual designs requiring future validation. The validation results show that the Physics-Informed Generative Adversarial Network (PI-GAN) generates ground motions with ≤ 5 % PGA error and ≤ 10 % response spectrum error, while the probabilistic damage cloud module achieves 77.7% overall classification accuracy (with 79.5% recall, 87.3% precision, and 83.2% F1-score) and 89.3% structure-damage matching degree. The framework enables a shift from empirical judgment to data-driven pre-simulation, providing a partially validated and technically feasible solution for improving the accuracy and comprehensiveness of urban seismic risk assessment, while clearly acknowledging that full-chain validation - particularly for extreme M≥ 7.0 scenarios and unvalidated modules - remains as future work.  © 2013 IEEE.

Source title: Materials and Manufacturing Processes

Authors with affiliations: Kolate V.D., Trinity Academy of Engineering, Pune and Savitribai Phule Pune University, Pune, India; Chaudhary M.K., Trinity Academy of Engineering, Pune and Savitribai Phule Pune University, Pune, India; Mane S., Trinity Academy of Engineering, Pune and Savitribai Phule Pune University, Pune, India; Devadhe M., Trinity Academy of Engineering, Pune and Savitribai Phule Pune University, Pune, India
Abstract: This review provides a comprehensive analysis of Digital Twin–enabled Model Predictive Control (DT–MPC) in Additive Manufacturing (AM), highlighting its potential to enable predictive, adaptive, and sustainable production. Digital twins–constructed using finite element models, data-driven surrogates, and hybrid physics-informed neural networks–offer dynamic, real-time process representation, while MPC provides optimal control under complex, multi-physics constraints. Comparative studies from 2015–2025 reveal significant advances in melt-pool stability, defect mitigation, and energy efficiency, though industrial adoption remains constrained by computational cost, synchronization lag, and limited interpretability. The proposed research roadmap identifies short-term goals in real-time scalability, mid-term objectives in uncertainty management and explainable AI, and long-term priorities in lifecycle-aware, eco-efficient manufacturing. Bridging these challenges requires standardized digital frameworks and interdisciplinary collaboration. DT–MPC emerges as a cornerstone of Industry 5.0—transforming AM into an intelligent, self-adaptive, and sustainable manufacturing paradigm. © 2025 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

Abstract: This paper investigates digital twin-aware task offloading in vehicular edge–cloud networks with stochastic arrivals and time-varying wireless channels, with the objective of minimizing long-term power consumption while ensuring delay-aware queue stability. We formulate an online joint control of the association, communication, and computation, and further propose a Lyapunov-guided deep reinforcement learning (LyDRL) algorithm. The algorithm adopts a two-stage controller, where a policy-based actor determines vehicle–server association, while a model-driven critic performs lightweight analytical updates of uplink bandwidth, offloaded tasks, and processing frequencies across the vehicle, edge, and cloud. These design choices result in three advantages: (i) virtual quality-of-service (QoS) queues enforce queue stability; (ii) a drift-plus-penalty weight makes the power–latency trade-off explicit and tunable; and (iii) digital twin prediction errors and channel uncertainty caused by imperfect channel state information (CSI) are embedded in the control state to improve robustness in online decision-making. Consequently, the decision routine runs in linear time per slot with modest memory overhead, enabling real-time deployment at scale over heterogeneous infrastructures. Trace-driven simulations on a 5 × 5 Manhattan grid demonstrate that LyDRL achieves rapid convergence and consistently outperforms purely data-driven DRL baselines. Specifically, it tightly bounds the physical and virtual queue backlogs at low levels under heavy traffic loads, minimizes system power consumption, and exhibits strong resilience against both digital twin prediction errors and CSI estimation errors. © 2000-2011 IEEE.

Abstract: Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks are becoming more complex as they require real-time decision-making and efficient resource management. These demands make it difficult to maintain stable and reliableoperations. The challenges are especially severe in dynamic and time-varying environments. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that integrates the quantum-based deep deterministic policy gradient (Q-DDPG) with digital twin networks (DTN) for distributed semantic optimization in dynamic IoV environments. The framework leverages quantum computing principles, such as superposition and entanglement, to enhance distributed semantic decisions. DTNs provide real-time modeling for efficient task offloading and adaptive resource allocation in decentralized IoV environments under varying conditions and uncertainties. The numerical results validate the robustness of the proposed approach, significantly reduce latency, and improve energy efficiency. © 2013 IEEE.

Abstract: Digital twin (DT) technology refers to high-fidelity, continuously updated virtual replicas of physical assets, processes, or systems. Originally developed in manufacturing, DTs are now expanding into agriculture. Agriculture presents unique challenges such as biophysical uncertainty, spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and socio-economic constraints. These conditions demand the integration of IoT sensing, edge and cloud computing, AI/ML simulations, and automated decision-making across farms and landscapes. This chapter examines the role of DTs in farming systems. First, it provides a historical and conceptual overview of digital twins in agriculture. Second, it introduces a reference architecture comprising perception, integration, modelling, analytics, and actuation layers. Third, it presents practical applications and case studies in precision irrigation, soil health, greenhouse climate control, and livestock management. Fourth, it highlights design considerations such as data standards, model fidelity, uncertainty quantification, and human-centred decision support. Evidence from pilot studies indicates that DTs can reduce water use by 15–30%, chemical inputs by 10–20%, and livestock sickness by 24–48%. They also improve yield prediction by 8–15%. The chapter concludes with a road map for developing interoperable, smallholder-inclusive, and climate-smart DTs that integrate both biophysical and socio-economic outcomes. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

Title: Mitigating Network Uncertainty in Rural Telesurgery: A Satellite-Driven Digital Twin Approach

Abstract: The delivery of telesurgical services to rural areas is hindered by unpredictable connectivity and limited infrastructure. While Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites offer promising low-latency coverage, their performance is vulnerable to visibility loss, handoffs, and link failures. To address this, we propose a Satellite Robotic Telesurgery Digital Twin (SRTDT) framework that integrates causal forecasting with a proxy-surgeon failover mechanism to ensure surgical continuity under network disruptions. Using twelve hours of simulated LEO data, we demonstrate: (i) a multitask deep learning model that predicts satellite visibility and failure types with 88% accuracy; (ii) a causal analysis linking orbital dynamics, such as: elevation, slant range, and path loss to the network KPIs including latency, jitter, throughput and packet loss; and (iii) an interpretable XGBoost+SHAP model that identifies elevation as a dominant driver of end to end delay, supported by Granger causality tests. In a simulated two-hour surgical procedure, our proactive failover mechanism recovered 57% of the execution time lost to network outages, enabling either a safe resumption or a controlled termination of the operation. These results underscore the potential of integrating causal forecasting with autonomous failover to mitigate the risks of satellite dependent telesurgery in remote settings. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Digital twins and resilience as mediators of climate change adaptation: Evidence from the non-renewable energy supply chain in India

Abstract: Climate change represents a significant challenge for non-renewable energy supply chains. Despite growing attention to climate change, limited research has examined how firms can leverage climate adaptation expenditures to improve supply chain efficiency. In existing literature, adaptation, digital tools, and resilience are often studied independently, with limited attention given to the interconnections among adaptation investments, digital twin technology adoption, and supply chain resilience. The model developed and tested in this study represents a serial mediation model grounded in the resource-based view and resource orchestration theory. The results demonstrate that climate adaptation investments positively influence supply chain management performance both directly and indirectly through digital twin technology adoption and supply chain resilience, including a sequential pathway from adaptation investment to digital twin technology adoption, to resilience, and ultimately to performance. Structural equation modeling was applied to analyze survey data collected from 306 participants in the non-renewable energy industry. The findings of the study indicate that climate change adaptation investments constitute strategic intangible resources, whose benefits are realized when firms develop complementary capabilities in digital twin technology adoption and supply chain resilience. Digital twins can help prioritize, simulate, and optimize adaptation strategies and resilience plans, providing managers with practical guidance for enhancing supply chain adaptability and resilience in the face of increasing climate uncertainty. © The Author(s) 2026. Abstract: Power distribution networks face increasing reliability challenges due to asset aging, growing penetration of distributed energy resources, and operational complexity. Existing predictive maintenance approaches generally have a single-modality data set, lack topology knowledge and provide limited physical consistency and uncertainty quantification, constraining early and reliable decision-making. This study aims to create and evaluate a digital twin-enabled, physicsinformed learning methodology to predictive maintenance of power distribution networks with high accuracy and uncertain predictions. A physics-guided graph digital twin (PHY-GDT) is used to conduct an experimental study which combines heterogeneous multimodal data, such as electrical telemetry, asset health indicators, environmental variables and topology via graph-transformer learning and differentiable power-flow constraints. The framework is trained and tested on publicly available datasets with standardized temporal splits, and evaluated against baseline (RF-LSTM) and hybrid (PI-GNN) models. PHY-GDT has a better performance in F1-score of 90.6% and PR-AUC of 88.7% compared to 72.4% / 68.2% with RF- LSTM. It allows much earlier detection of failures, the median lead time decreases to 48 h (vs 6h baseline), the RUL RMSE decreases to 9.1 days, and delivers well-calibrated uncertainty (PICP=0.89). Operationally, it yields 3.9 ×-4.2 × higher expected avoided outage costs. The findings indicate that a combination of multimodal data, topology and physics in a digital twin can significantly improve the predictive maintenance accuracy and reliability to facilitate risk-conscious and proactive utility operation.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The integration of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) with Digital Twin (DT) frameworks offers a transformative pathway for modern bridge management, enabling satellite-data selection of structures to engage decision-making across the asset life cycle. This approach supports proactive Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), prioritization of predictive maintenance (PM) over repair and rehabilitation interventions, and enhanced informed planning. Therefore, promising case studies demonstrating the practicability of fusing satellite-derived displacement data with Building Information Modelling (BIM), based digital representations, taking into consideration several barriers, such as semantic interoperability, uncertainty quantification, real-time data assimilation, and institutional integration into Bridge Management Systems (BMS). This work outlines a systematic framework for implementing InSAR-enhanced digital twins according to a literature review, emphasizing their role in integration with BIM, lifecycle administration, and predictive assurance. By synthesizing recent advances and identifying key research gaps, this contribution aligns with ongoing international efforts to standardize and operationalize digital twin adoption for sustainable, resilient, and optimized bridge infrastructure management. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Robust Data-Driven Control for Nonlinear Systems Using their Digital Twins and Quadratic Funnels
Source title: Proceedings of the American Control Conference
Affiliations: University of Washington, Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics, United States
Authors with affiliations: Shakeri S., University of Washington, Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics, United States; Mesbahi M., University of Washington, Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics, United States
Abstract: This paper examines a robust data-driven approach for the safe deployment of systems with nonlinear dynamics using their imperfect digital twins. Our contribution involves proposing a method that fuses the digital twin's nominal trajectory with online, data-driven uncertainty quantification to synthesize robust tracking controllers. Specifically, we derive data-driven bounds to capture the deviations of the actual system from its prescribed nominal trajectory informed via its digital twin. Subsequently, the dataset is used in the synthesis of quadratic funnels - robust positive invariant tubes around the nominal trajectory - via linear matrix inequalities built on the time-series data. The resulting controller guarantees constraint satisfaction while adapting to the true system behavior through a segmented learning strategy, where each segment's controller is synthesized using uncertainty information from the previous segment. This work establishes a systematic framework for obtaining safety certificates in learning-based control of nonlinear systems with imperfect models.  © 2026 AACC.

Title: Agentic artificial intelligence-driven digital twin for real-time irrigation control with fuzzy sustainability objectives
Source title: International Journal of Optimization and Control: Theories and Applications
Affiliations: Industrial Business Department, Business Faculty, University of National and World Economy, Sofia, Bulgaria
Authors with affiliations: Nozari H., Industrial Business Department, Business Faculty, University of National and World Economy, Sofia, Bulgaria; Yordanova Z., Industrial Business Department, Business Faculty, University of National and World Economy, Sofia, Bulgaria
Abstract: Irrigation management in modern agriculture faces simultaneous challenges, including water scarcity, climate uncertainty, and the need for long-term sustainability. In this study, an integrated framework for real-time irrigation control is presented, in which a digital twin is not merely used as a monitoring or simulation tool but is directly embedded in the decision-making and control loop through an agent-based fuzzy multi-objective optimization mechanism. Unlike conventional smart irrigation approaches that rely on static thresholds or offline optimization, the proposed framework enables adaptive, context-based decision updates by continuously integrating physical system feedback into a dynamic optimization engine. The decision-making agent, by simultaneously assessing soil, climate, and plant growth conditions, generates irrigation policies that balance water consumption, crop growth, and environmental sustainability requirements under fuzzy uncertainty. Experimental results show that using dynamic feedback in the digital twin framework improves the multi-objective performance index by more than 12% compared to the static state and significantly reduces control fluctuations. Convergence, stability under uncertainty, and parameter sensitivity analyses also indicate that the proposed framework can establish a sustainable balance across water resource utilization, crop yield, and environmental considerations. The findings indicate that this approach can provide a practical and reliable platform for transitioning to smart, adaptive, and sustainable irrigation systems. Title: Digital Twins in Oncology: From Multimodal Data Integration to Precision Clinical Practice
Source title: Indian Journal of Radiology and Imaging
Affiliations: Madha Medical College and Research Institute, Tamil Nadu, Thandalam, India; Department of Medical Sciences and Technology, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Authors with affiliations: Vairavan A., Madha Medical College and Research Institute, Tamil Nadu, Thandalam, India; Bhattacharjee R., Department of Medical Sciences and Technology, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India; Raghavan B., Department of Medical Sciences and Technology, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Abstract: Oncology digital twins are patient-specific computational models that are built by combining electronic health records, multiomics genomic data, and diagnostic imaging to simulate individual tumor biology and predict multiple treatment-related outcomes. Conceptually originated from aerospace engineering, it has matured clinically through convergent advances in radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic- pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and, most recently, large language model (LLM)-based clinical interfaces and agentic artificial intelligence (AI). For a practicing radiologist, digital twins offer a transformative role: imaging-derived quantitative features serve as the primary data, positioning diagnostic imaging at the center of these personalized oncology workflows. Key clinical applications especially in oncology span from chemotherapy response prediction, immunotherapy patient selection, personalized radiation planning, tumor progression modeling, and treatment toxicity forecasting. Several of these applications are achievable with current technology without any significant infrastructure investment. Substantial challenges include imaging data standards, absence of prospective validation, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, and regulatory uncertainty for continuously self-updating AI. This narrative review provides radiologists with a balanced, comprehensive overview of digital twin architecture, advanced enabling technologies, current clinical evidence, a practical roadmap for implementation, and a candid appraisal of barriers to adoption. © 2026 Indian Radiological Association. Title: Edge-assisted Digital Twin-integrated Architecture for Crop Recommendation in Smart Agriculture
Source title: IEEE Journal on Selected Topics in Signal Processing
Affiliations: National Institute of Technology, Delhi, India; University of Washington, Seattle, United States; Indian Institute of Information Technology, Una, India; Indiamart, India
Authors with affiliations: Kaur A., National Institute of Technology, Delhi, India; Sahil S., National Institute of Technology, Delhi, India; Chenab C., University of Washington, Seattle, United States; Kumar S., Indian Institute of Information Technology, Una, India, Indiamart, India
Abstract: Proper agricultural practices, and appropriate edaphological and environmental conditions ensure a substantial agri-productions. However, the uncertainty and variability in these factors, often leads to inefficient and low productivity. To address this issue, data-driven intelligence-assisted informed decision making can be considered a prominent tool that would enhance the performance and sustainability in agriculture domain. This work proposes a Predictive Digital Twin that utilizes Edge-Cloud-assisted collaborative intelligence built upon soil and weather data for providing on-time and contextual analytics related to Soil Health Alerts, Soil Type Identification, Weather Forecasting and Crop Recommendations, enabling concerned stakeholders for enhanced agriculture outputs. The work utilizes a layered architecture for Digital Twin that employs Edge-assisted Kernel K-Means Clustering for Nutrient-based Edaphological Variability Analysis and XGBoost for Soil Type Identification, and Cloud-assisted Temporal Fusion Transformers (TFT) for Weather Forecasting and TabNet for Crop Recommendations. The work also proposes an adaptive information-aware transmission strategy for the energy conservation of sensor nodes, required in the agriculture field settings. The experimental evaluation clearly depicts the effectiveness of the proposed Digital Twin approach for Crop Recommendation and Energy Conservation of sensor node. © 2007-2012 IEEE.

Abstract: Electric bus fleet optimization, including scheduling and charging, relies on vehicle telemetry transmitted over vehicular communication networks. However, communication uncertainty in these networks, including packet loss, can degrade or interrupt data availability, compromising the reliability of decision-making. Since fleet optimization is globally coupled across multiple buses, missing data from even a subset of vehicles can lead to suboptimal or infeasible decisions. In this work, we propose a digital twin framework for optimizing electric bus operations, which accounts for communication uncertainty and maintains reliable fleet performance under incomplete telemetry. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Generative Framework for Supply Chain Digital Twins: Simulating and Optimizing Logistics Scenarios Using AI-Generated Data and Rules

Affiliations: Project Lead for Modern Applications, Applied Medical Resources, Rancho Mission Viejo, CA, United States
