Abstract: The visibly quickened globalization of the trade and the ever more intricate network of supply chains require some innovative ways of providing predictive analysis, real-time optimization, and testing scenarios. Conventional methods of supply chain modelling have been known to be challenged by unfinished data, unpredictable demand and evolving interference like geopolitical disturbance, natural calamity as well as abrupt market variability. To answer this question, the paper suggests a generative model of Supply Chain Digital Twins (SCDTs), an information system that combines artificial intelligence (AI)-generated synthetic samples and rule-based learning to generate and support the optimization of logistics. The structure builds on generative adversarial networks (GANs), reinforcement learning and executing a constraint-based model to build and develop dynamic virtual copies of analogous supply chains. The framework can enable its stakeholders to test the operational strategies in unpredictable and stressful situations by coming up with realistic patterns, delays on the roads, and difference in inventory. The comparison experiment demonstrates that AI-based digital twins are more adaptable and robust over conventional simulation systems, especially in terms of coping with the last-mile deliveries issues and supplier uncertainties. Although the framework offers a sizeable and adaptable method of supply chain optimization, active constraints can be assessed in regard to the cost of computation, its ability to integrate with existing enterprise frameworks, and also in the ethical repercussions of excessive use of synthetic data. Future directions of model interpretability and the combination of generative models with real-time IoT rivers and the development of standardized protocols that enable cross-industry use of supply chains digital twins should also be addressed in future research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Multimodal Ontology: Semantic Substrate for Human Digital Twins in AI-Driven Metaverse Telerehabilitation and Immersive Medical Education

Abstract: The convergence of the metaverse with AI and digital twin technologies is reshaping healthcare delivery and medical education, yet Human Digital Twins (HDTs) – continuously updated virtual patient models – often lack a unifying semantic substrate capable of integrating heterogeneous multimodal evidence (sensor streams, clinical text, imaging, and interaction traces) into actionable meaning for perception, reasoning, and decision support. This viewpoint positions multimodal ontology as that substrate and as a prerequisite for robust AI-driven metaverse workflows in telerehabilitation and immersive medical education. Multimodal ontology is defined at a high level of abstraction and specified via a minimal formalization capturing its essential elements: domain concepts and relations, modality sets, semantic grounding operators that map raw observations to ontological entities, and state-update functions that maintain a temporally evolving HDT knowledge state. Building on recent HDT-enabled telerehabilitation work, the ontology layer is shown to operationalize core metaverse AI functions – environmental perception, semantic understanding, behavioral planning, and human–machine collaboration through interoperable representations, rule-and graph-based inference, and explainable agent behavior across clinician, patient, and intern interfaces. A testable research agenda is outlined for ontology-backed HDTs, emphasizing integration with large-scale multimodal models, validation in simulation and real-world deployments, and evaluation using semantic consistency, reasoning fidelity, user trust, and patient or intern outcomes. The specific contribution is not a new classifier, simulator, or network-optimization mechanism; rather, it is a formal semantic substrate that couples multimodal grounding, confidence-weighted fusion, uncertainty-aware HDT state evolution, and ontology-constrained interaction with large-scale foundation models. © 2026 by author(s). Abstract: Accurately estimating parameters of physiological models is essential to achieving reliable digital twins. For Type 1 Diabetes, this is particularly challenging due to the complexity of glucose–insulin interactions. Traditional methods based on Markov Chain Monte Carlo struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces and fit parameters from scratch at inference time, making them slow and computationally expensive. In this study, we propose a Simulation-Based Inference approach based on Neural Posterior Estimation to efficiently capture the complex relationships between meal intake, insulin, and glucose level, providing faster, amortized inference. Our experiments demonstrate that SBI not only outperforms traditional methods in parameter estimation but also generalizes better to unseen conditions, offering real-time posterior inference with reliable uncertainty quantification. Title: Digital twin framework for structural health monitoring using PWT-excited Lamb waves
Source title: Mechanics of Advanced Materials and Structures
Affiliations: Department of Aerospace Engineering, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Kerala, Trivandrum, India
Authors with affiliations: Harikumar V., Department of Aerospace Engineering, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Kerala, Trivandrum, India; Bijudas C.R., Department of Aerospace Engineering, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Kerala, Trivandrum, India
Abstract: Non-destructive structural health monitoring (SHM) employs techniques that allow for the continuous evaluation of structural integrity without causing harm to the structure itself. By utilising methods such as Lamb wave propagation and detection using piezoelectric wafer transducer (PWT), these systems enable the early detection of defects or damage, ensuring the safety and longevity of critical infrastructure. PWTs are employed to generate and detect guided waves, such as Lamb waves (LW), within the structures. These waves propagate through the structure, and the responses can be analysed to identify the presence of damage. Nonetheless, damage identification via damage-sensitive features derived from diverse signal processing techniques may prove ineffective in real-world settings characterised by several uncertainties. To address these challenges, a digital twin model that accommodates these uncertainties in SHM using PWAS is presented. The bonding between the sensor and the structure can significantly impact SHM applications where partial contact loss may lead to incorrect conclusions, potentially being misinterpreted as damage within the structure. A data-driven approach is implemented to develop a digital twin (DT) model that distinguishes between healthy and damaged states. Experimental studies are conducted with a wafer-type sensor coupled to an elastic plate, and a laser vibrometer is used as a receiver to analyse the A0 mode behaviour at different points within a 30 cm radius surrounding the sensor. Mode tuning curves for a frequency range from 13 kHz to 260 kHz are obtained, with the amplitude found to vary with bonding conditions. The obtained response is then used to train the digital twin model, which can be further tested with damage scenarios. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, N V R Naidu, K R V Subramanian, Nagaraju Kottam and G N Anil Kumar, individual chapters, the contributors.

Title: Predict First, Sync When Needed: A Risk-Aware Approach to Adaptive Digital Twin Synchronization Under Bandwidth Constraints
Source title: Proceedings of IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium, NOMS 2026
Affiliations: University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland; Eurecom, Department Of Communication Systems, France
Authors with affiliations: Wanigarathna Y.R., University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland; Tarkoma S., University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland; Morabito R., University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland, Eurecom, Department Of Communication Systems, France
Abstract: Maintaining real-time synchronization between physical assets and their Digital Twins over bandwidth-limited wireless links is a complex challenge. Existing approaches either transmit all sensed data, resulting in unnecessary network overhead, or rely solely on forecasting, which cannot guarantee fidelity when operating conditions change. In response, we present a risk-aware, event-driven synchronization framework that leverages predictive modeling to minimize network traffic while maintaining the fidelity of digital twins. Our approach utilizes a Gated Recurrent Unit-based quantile forecaster to predict key states with calibrated uncertainty. Additionally, it employs online quantile coverage and Kullback-Leibler divergence tests to monitor reliability and detect changes in distribution. The system operates in a predictive mode, fetching only selected states, and shifts to full synchronization and model retraining when deviations are detected. We conducted experiments using public LTE and 5G datasets, achieving R2>0.80 in most cases, with a peak of 0.99. Real-world evaluations using a commercial smartphone showed network-traffic reductions of 5. 4-7. 0 % versus continuous synchronization, along with mean absolute error (MAE) reductions of about 64% on average relative to simpler predictive methods. These findings demonstrate that predictive synchronization, coupled with awareness of drift, enables highfidelity digital twinning even under strict bandwidth constraints. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This work presents a digital twin framework for angular error compensation in a high-precision rotary table. The approach exploits continuous interaction between the physical rotary table and its virtual counterpart, where the physical system provides real-time measurements from a dual encoder, thermal probes, and capacitive sensors representative of the actual operating state. These measurements are fused in a particle-filter-based data assimilation module. The virtual rotary table is continuously updated and incorporates three complementary models: a geometrical error model, a thermal drift model, and sensor error models. By synchronizing the virtual entity with the physical system, the framework estimates the true angular position and delivers a corrected angle in real time. This corrected angle is used for metrological evaluation or fed back into the control loop. © 2026 EUSPEN. All Rights Reserved.

Abstract: Remote patient monitoring systems for cardiovascular care often employ deterministic models that produce singular risk projections based on static clinical observations. The existing approaches have fallen short in capturing the uncertainty of a patient's condition and how their disease or conditions may evolve in the possible future. To address this gap this paper presents a Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) based Cardiac Digital Twin framework that learns a compact, meaningful representation of each patient and every and uses it to simulate possible future physiological states. Patient data is first encoded into a latent representation using an autoencoder, which also serves as the patient's digital twin. This latent space is then used to train a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate multiple realistic future cardiac scenarios. Alongside this, a supervised risk prediction model estimates mortality risk for both real patient data and the generated future states. Experimental results show that the framework maintains strong predictive performance while significantly improving coverage by accounting for different possible future outcomes. These findings have highlighted the potential of latent space digital-Twins to enable more proactive and uncertainty aware remote monitoring of cardiac patients.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: To address scheduling delays caused by dynamic order insertion, processing-time uncertainty, machine abnormality, and load imbalance in intelligent workshops, this paper proposes a digital twin workshop active scheduling method based on spatio-temporal Transformer prediction. The core novelty is a closed-loop mechanism that couples graph-based digital twin state updating, topology-masked spatio-temporal risk prediction, and benefit-cost risk-triggered adjustment, so that schedules are changed only before high-impact risks become critical. First, real-time workshop data are synchronized into a digital twin and represented as a spatio-temporal graph consisting of machines, operations, orders, and buffers. Then, a spatio-temporal Transformer learns structural dependencies among workshop entities and temporal evolution of production states. The model predicts future machine load, queue length, order delay probability, and bottleneck risk. Based on these predictions, candidate schedules are generated and verified through digital twin simulation before execution. Experiments on Brandimarte and Taillard benchmarks with dynamic disturbances show that the proposed method improves risk prediction accuracy, reduces order delay rate, and decreases unnecessary rescheduling compared with dispatching rules, LSTM-based predictive scheduling, and conventional Transformer-based predictive scheduling.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: With the increasing complexity of equipment management, equipment digital twin technology, as an innovative management tool, is becoming an essential means to improve the efficiency of equipment lifecycle management. Abstract: Fast ray tracing (RT) has stimulated the digital twin (DT) as an emerging technology for environment-aware communications. Since wireless propagation is governed by the site geometry and electromagnetic (EM) properties of the environment, DT provides a site-specific prior for channel estimation. In this work, we investigate the robustness of DT in pilot-based channel estimation, where multipath features extracted via RT determine the low-rank (LR) eigenstructure of the channel covariance. However, inaccuracies in the digital representation perturb this eigenstructure. We analyze positioning and EM calibration errors and derive a first-order perturbative model that separates geometric perturbations, affecting angles and delays, from EM calibration perturbations, affecting path gains. The normalized mean-square error (NMSE) analysis reveals a fundamental asymmetry. LR estimation is inherently robust to EM calibration perturbations, while positioning errors dominate performance degradation by altering the channel eigenstructure. Numerical results confirm that positioning errors are the primary limiting factor in the urban scenario, with consistent behavior across suburban and rural scenarios, whereas EM calibration errors have a limited impact. Nonetheless, DT-empowered estimators provide up to 10: dB NMSE improvement over baseline methods in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) urban settings and remain comparable to baseline estimators at high SNR for moderate (< 1: m) positioning errors.  © 1972-2012 IEEE.

Abstract: In the field of heritage conservation and preservation, the integration of digital tools has transformed the approach to management, maintenance and renovation of existing buildings. Digital Building Logbooks (DBLs) and Digital Twin (DT) technologies have the potential to support the assessment and the monitoring of structural performance, in order to identify vulnerability and to enable better decision making throughout the building lifespan. In this study, a framework is proposed for developing structural DTs to monitor the dynamic behavior of heritage buildings. The framework initiates with data gathered from DBLs and encompasses the generation of Heritage Building Information Models (H-BIM) derived from digital surveys. Subsequently, three-dimensional finite element models (FEM) are generated and calibrated. This approach addresses the challenges associated with interoperability, particularly those related to the reproduction of complex geometries, the assignment of material properties and the generation of accurate shells for the development of FE models. Finally, the possibility to derive analytical response surfaces reproducing the dynamic behavior of the building is investigated in view of quantifying uncertainties, evaluating sensitivities and monitoring changes in the predicted behavior. The proposed methodology will be illustrated with reference to a significant case study, Palazzo Poniatowski-Guadagni, a 18th-century masonry building in Florence. The resulting digital twin will be integrated into the BUILDCHAIN system, which seeks to illustrate the advantages of utilising innovative digital building logbooks for the effective management and preservation of cultural heritage. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: The healthcare sector faces complex challenges exacerbated by tight timelines and fragmented data. Uncertainty, underutilized resources, overcrowding and inadequate information are common problems for decision-makers. In resolving such matters, a Digital Twin, a detailed digital replica of the healthcare system, offers a promising solution. This technology models patient inflows and determines congestion levels and resource and service use to simulate, forecast, and optimize healthcare behaviors. We show the reliability of our system by modelling a complex organization such as one of the Local Health Authority (ASL) of Tuscany. Our Digital Twin system could enable proactive and deliberative-driven decisions by supporting the evaluation of system impacts and optimizing resource utilization. Moreover, the Digital Twin enhances system resilience while improving the decision-making process with the additional data provided through feedback. Such a tool may enable better strategic and optimal resource use. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2026.

Abstract: Influenced by complex environmental loads, the mechanical properties of structures evolve throughout their service life. Accurately identifying the characteristic parameters of inservice structures and evaluating their safety performance remain major challenges. This study proposes a hierarchical Bayesian dynamic updating method for time-varying reliability assessment tailored to structural dynamic digital twins. A digital twin model of the physical structure is first established using finite element theory. Based on the monitored dynamic responses of the physical structure, the modal parameters of the digital model are identified through Bayesian inference. A hierarchical Bayesian framework is then constructed to estimate the time-varying physical parameters, whose statistical characteristics are extracted using the expectation-maximization algorithm. The digital model is subsequently updated using the principle of maximum entropy. Leveraging probability density evolution theory, a new approach for evaluating the dynamic reliability of time-varying structures is developed. Compared with traditional methods, the proposed method more comprehensively accounts for the temporal variability of service-related parameters and their associated uncertainties. The effectiveness of the approach is validated through numerical studies on shear-type structures, bridge models, and laboratory experiments, with comparisons drawn against conventional methods. Results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a more accurate acquisition of the parameters of the digital model and significantly improves the handling of parameter variability, thus ensuring the robustness of structural dynamic reliability assessment results. © (2026), (Chang’an University). Title: Production planning with digital twins

Abstract: In Industry 4.0, manufacturers increasingly use digital twins (DTs) to develop real-time representations of shop floors. However, the application of DTs in production planning remains limited. This paper proposes a DT-driven methodology for production planning that integrates planning engines, simulation, forecasting, and data-driven models. The decision model is formulated as a multi-echelon, multi-item capacitated lot-sizing problem (MMCLSP). The DT improves model fidelity by extracting key parameters and characterizing uncertainties from historical and real-time data. We extend the deterministic MMCLSP to a stochastic formulation for demand uncertainty, and, introduce a closed-loop mechanism that updates production lead times using simulation feedback. Two industrial case studies demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively integrates aggregate production planning with shop-floor execution. Compared with deterministic approaches, the stochastic model with data-driven lead times yields more effective and operationally feasible production plans, enhancing decision support for manufacturing systems. © 2026 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

Title: Improving Response Time and System Resilience in Humanitarian Supply Chains Using Digital Twin and Fuzzy Multi-Objective Optimization
Source title: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability
Affiliations: University of national and world economy, Sofia, Bulgaria
Authors with affiliations: Nozari H., University of national and world economy, Sofia, Bulgaria; Yordanova Z., University of national and world economy, Sofia, Bulgaria
Abstract: Humanitarian supply chains in crisis situations face high uncertainty, infrastructure disruption, and severe time pressure; therefore, decision-making in these environments requires a framework that can simultaneously manage response speed, operational efficiency, performance stability, and network resilience. This research presents an integrated framework based on multi-objective optimization, fuzzy uncertainty modeling, and digital twin to allocate and distribute relief resources in unstable environments in a dynamic, data-driven manner, supporting operational stability. The results showed that the proposed model reduced response time by 30.6% and total cost by 17.1% compared to the baseline, while increasing service level by 25.8% and resilience index by 58.3%. Also, the integration of digital twin resulted in a reduction of response time by 21.6% and demand shortfall by 44.9%. Scenario, Pareto and sensitivity analyses also confirmed the robustness, interpretability and reliability of the model. The findings indicate that the proposed framework can be an effective basis for designing smart, flexible, resilient and sustainable relief networks in crisis situations. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

Authors: Choi D.; Wang X.; Mirbod O.
Title: Smart Sensing and Digital Twin Technology for Yield Estimation and Phenomics Prediction in Strawberries
Source title: Smart Agriculture: Concepts, Strategies, and Case Studies
Affiliations: University of Florida, Wimauma, FL, United States
Authors with affiliations: Choi D., University of Florida, Wimauma, FL, United States; Wang X., University of Florida, Wimauma, FL, United States; Mirbod O., University of Florida, Wimauma, FL, United States
Abstract: Strawberry is a popular and economically significant fruit worldwide, with a substantial volume produced and consumed globally. However, it faces various production challenges including labor shortages, weather uncertainties, competition from imports, disease outbreaks, and insect infestations. This chapter explores the use of smart sensing for yield estimation, phenomics prediction for trait analysis, and digital twin technology for virtual simulation to enhance strawberry production. The implementation steps for each technique are discussed and examples of successful applications in strawberry production are given. These digital techniques provide a perspective of crop conditions, assisting in optimizing management practices, improving productivity and profitability, and promoting sustainable agriculture. However, their adoption also brings about certain challenges like high costs and the necessity for standardized data collection and analysis protocols. Additionally, the chapter emphasizes the importance of collaborative efforts among industry stakeholders for fostering innovation and encouraging the adoption of these technologies. © 2026 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

Abstract: Precision livestock farming requires accurate and timely heat stress prediction to ensure animal welfare and optimize farm management. This study presents a physics-informed digital twin (DT) framework combined with an uncertainty-aware, expert-weighted stacked ensemble for multimodal forecasting of Core Body Temperature (CBT) in dairy cattle. Using the high-frequency, heterogeneous MmCows dataset, the DT integrates an ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based thermoregulation model that simulates metabolic heat production and dissipation, a Gaussian process for capturing cow-specific deviations, a Kalman filter for aligning predictions with real-time sensor data, and a behavioral Markov chain that models activity-state transitions under varying environmental conditions. The DT outputs key physiological indicators, such as predicted CBT, heat stress probability, and behavioral state distributions are fused with raw sensor data and enriched through multi-scale temporal analysis and cross-modal feature engineering to form a comprehensive feature set. The predictive methodology is designed in a three-stage stacked ensemble, where stage 1 trains modality-specific LightGBM ‘expert’ models on distinct feature groups, stage 2 collects their predictions as meta-features, and at stage 3 Optuna-tuned LightGBM meta-model yields the final CBT forecast. Predictive uncertainty is quantified via bootstrapping and validated using Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP). Ablation analysis confirms that incorporating DT-derived features and multimodal fusion substantially enhances performance. The proposed framework achieves a cross-validated R2 of 0.783, F1 score of 84.25% and PICP of 92.38% for 2-hour ahead forecasting, providing a robust, uncertainty-aware, and physically principled system for early heat stress detection and precision livestock management. © 2026

Title: AUGMENTED DECISION-MAKING IN VENTURE CAPITAL: INTEGRATING DIGITAL TWINS AND AI-BASED MARKET INTELLIGENCE
Source title: ECONOMICS - Innovative and Economics Research Journal

Authors with affiliations: Yordanova Z., University of National and World Economy, Industrial Business Department, Sofia, Bulgaria; Nozari H., University of National and World Economy, Institute for Economics and Politics, Sofia, Bulgaria
Abstract: Venture capital decision-making is increasingly influenced by uncertainty, information asymmetry, and the growing volume of unstructured data. Although previous research has advanced analytical methods for portfolio selection, existing approaches rarely integrate dynamic system behaviour with qualitative market intelligence within a unified framework. This study proposes an AI-augmented decision framework that combines digital twins with large language model-based market intelligence to support venture capital investment under uncertainty. The framework integrates structured financial data with real-time qualitative insights from market narratives, while digital twins simulate startup development and scenario-based performance. Embedded within a multi-criteria decision structure, these inputs enable more adaptive, transparent, and interpretable portfolio selection. Empirical findings indicate that the proposed framework improves decision quality by increasing expected returns while reducing risk and prediction error. It also strengthens decision stability and supports more effective evaluation of trade-offs in complex investment environments. The study contributes to the literature on AI-enabled decision-making and innovation finance by demonstrating how emerging technologies can improve investment evaluation and reduce uncertainty in entrepreneurial ecosystems. © 2026 ECONOMICS.

Title: Unveiling the potential of digital twins in homecare: A reflexive thematic analysis of older adults’ views
Source title: Digital Health
Affiliations: School of Health and Welfare, Dalarna University, Falun, Sweden; Post Graduate School for Integrated Care, Örebro University, Örebro, Sweden
Authors with affiliations: Saade S., School of Health and Welfare, Dalarna University, Falun, Sweden, Post Graduate School for Integrated Care, Örebro University, Örebro, Sweden; Nordin S., School of Health and Welfare, Dalarna University, Falun, Sweden; McKee K., School of Health and Welfare, Dalarna University, Falun, Sweden; Elf M., School of Health and Welfare, Dalarna University, Falun, Sweden; Borg J., School of Health and Welfare, Dalarna University, Falun, Sweden
Abstract: Objectives: A growing number of frail older adults live at home, placing increasing demands on health and social care systems. Digital twins may improve homecare services and support person-centred and integrated care. This study investigated older adults’ experiences of homecare and their perspectives on the potential use of digital twins in homecare. Methods: An exploratory, two-stage qualitative study was conducted with 14 older adults from two Swedish municipalities. In the first stage, semi-structured interviews explored participants’ experiences of homecare. In the second stage, the same participants took part in either a semi-structured interview or a focus group discussion regarding their views on digital twins, with participants choosing their preferred format. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to interpret the data. Results: The analysis generated one main theme, Navigating uncertainty and possibility in digital twin-supported homecare, with four sub-themes, Challenges in understanding and accepting digital twins, Concerns about privacy and ethics, Opportunities for safety and prevention, and Potential effects on daily routines. Participants struggled to comprehend the nature of digital twins. Concerns about their potential use in homecare included ethical issues, impacts on privacy, and reduced social interaction with homecare staff. However, participants also identified potential benefits of digital twins, such as more responsive services, improved scheduling, and enhanced safety through monitoring and predictive functions. Conclusion: This study highlights the potential of digital twins in homecare from the perspective of older adults. While digital twins offer opportunities, integrating them into homecare services is complex and requires addressing the concerns raised by participants. © The Author(s) 2026. Title: Hybrid and Multifunctional Asphalt Pavements: An Evidence-Based Review of Computational Intelligence, Digital Twins, and Circular Deployment
Source title: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Thamar University, Dhamar, Yemen; Department of Civil Engineering, National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Balochistan Campus, Quetta, Pakistan
Authors with affiliations: Alnadish A.M., Department of Civil Engineering, Thamar University, Dhamar, Yemen, Department of Civil Engineering, National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Balochistan Campus, Quetta, Pakistan; Waheed A., Department of Civil Engineering, National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Balochistan Campus, Quetta, Pakistan
Abstract: This review examines hybrid and multifunctional asphalt modifiers for enhancing pavement performance and sustainability. By integrating polymers, nanomaterials, and waste-derived fillers, these systems generate multiphase networks that improve rutting resistance, fatigue tolerance, and low-temperature flexibility, while multifunctional additives enable self-healing and self-sensing capabilities. Recycled and bio-based materials can reduce environmental impacts when they substitute virgin inputs and extend service life, but laboratory gains remain constrained by interfacial compatibility, dispersion quality, aging sensitivity, and scale-up uncertainty. Advanced characterization, molecular modelling, numerical simulation, machine learning, and digital-twin concepts provide tools for formulation optimization, condition prediction, preventive maintenance, and field-performance updating. The review further introduces a methodologically conservative analytical layer, including a worked homogeneous pooled subset, a conservative Synergy Index example, decision-support equations, LCA/LCCA metrics, a Circularity-Adjusted Synergy Index, a critical digital-twin evidence synthesis, and recommendations for standards bodies. Overall, hybrid and multifunctional asphalt modifiers provide a strategic route toward durable, low-carbon pavements, provided that claims are supported by reproducible data, field validation, and transparent circularity assessment. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to International Center for Numerical Methods in Engineering (CIMNE) 2026.

Title: Digital Twins for Cows and Chickens: From Hype Cycles to Hard Evidence in Precision Livestock Farming
Source title: Agriculture (Switzerland)
Affiliations: Faculty of Computer Science, Dalhousie University, Halifax, B3H 4R2, NS, Canada; Faculty of Agriculture, Dalhousie University, Truro, B3H 4R2, NS, Canada
Authors with affiliations: Neethirajan S., Faculty of Computer Science, Dalhousie University, Halifax, B3H 4R2, NS, Canada, Faculty of Agriculture, Dalhousie University, Truro, B3H 4R2, NS, Canada
Abstract: Digital twin technology is widely promoted as a transformative step for precision livestock farming, yet no fully realized, engineering-grade digital twins are deployed in commercial dairy or poultry systems today. This work establishes the current state of knowledge on dairy and poultry digital twins by synthesizing evidence through systematic database searches, thematic evidence mapping and critical analysis of validation gaps, carbon accounting and adoption barriers. Existing platforms are better described as near-digital-twin systems with partial sensing and modelling, digital-twin-inspired prototypes, simulation frameworks or decision-support tools that are often labelled as twins despite lacking continuous synchronization and closed-loop control. This distinction matters because the empirical foundation supporting many claims remains limited. Three critical gaps emerge: life-cycle carbon impacts of digital infrastructures are rarely quantified even as sustainability benefits are frequently asserted; field-validated improvements in feed efficiency, particularly in poultry feed conversion ratios, are scarce and inconsistent; and systematic reporting of failure rates, downtime and technology abandonment is almost absent, leaving uncertainties about long-term reliability. Adoption barriers persist across technical, economic and social dimensions, including rural connectivity limitations, sensor durability challenges, capital and operating costs, and farmer concerns regarding data rights, transparency and trust. Progress for cows and chickens will require rigorous validation in commercial environments, integration of mechanistic and statistical modelling, open and modular architectures and governance structures that support biological, economic and environmental accountability whilst ensuring that system intelligence is worth its material and energy cost. © 2026 by the author.

Abstract: This paper presents an integrated workflow that combines building information modelling, digital twins, earlystage energy screening, and probabilistic project controls to support construction decisions that balance delivery risk and carbon performance. The study uses the open ENB2012 benchmark dataset of 768 simulated building design cases to train a surrogate model that predicts heating and cooling demand and enables rapid screening of envelope alternatives during concept development; accordingly, the reported numerical results should be interpreted as a reproducible proof-of-concept rather than project-specific performance estimates. A risk simulation model is then applied to a calibrated register of cost and schedule events under four levels of digital maturity, ranging from traditional delivery to governed use of building information modelling, digital twins, and generative artificial intelligence. Across 40,000 simulation iterations for each scenario, greater digital maturity consistently reduces average overruns and extreme outcomes, lowering the ninetieth percentile schedule delay from about 48 days to about 31 days and reducing mean cost overrun from about 10.8 percent to about 8.3 percent for a representative retrofit programme, while preserving the operational carbon benefits of envelope upgrades. The study contributes a transparent and reproducible decision framework that links information governance, design evaluation, and uncertainty analysis, and it concludes with a practical implementation pathway for organisations operating in resource-constrained environments.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Digital Twins of Cities: Modeling Urban Dynamics and Complexity
Source title: Advances in Spatial Science

Abstract: As cities evolve at unprecedented speed and scale, traditional digital twins—virtual models of physical urban systems—fall short in capturing the dynamic and complex nature of urban life. This book bridges the gap between digital urban representations and the dynamic processes that shape our cities. Moving beyond conventional data and technological infrastructure, this work formulates a comprehensive framework for embedding urban dynamics and complexity into digital twins. It reimagines them as living systems that adapt, learn and evolve in real time, near real time and over the long horizon. Through integrated feedback loops between data, physical infrastructure, high-dimensional models and reduced-order approximations, digital twins are transformed into powerful tools for the modeling, simulation, prediction and proactive management of urban development. This book presents cutting-edge methods to learn, simplify and encode urban dynamics and complexity into digital twins—whether or not the underlying mechanisms are fully understood. It also addresses critical challenges such as scalability, uncertainty propagation, network sensing and data quality, and demonstrates how dynamic digital twins can be continually refined through new information and emerging insights. At the intersection of urban theory, artificial intelligence, machine learning and big spatiotemporal data, this book charts a new course for the modeling and governance of cities. It is a vital resource for researchers, practitioners and decision-makers across disciplines—inviting collaboration between academia, industry, government and professionals working on the frontlines of our ever-changing urban environments. Explore a bold vision for cities that can think, adapt and respond—one where digital twins become not just mirrors, but engines of transformation. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Digital Twin-Based Geometric Error Modeling and Inverse Kinematics Compensation for 5-Axis CNC Machining

Affiliations: German International University, Department of Robotics Engineering, New Administrative Capital, Egypt
Authors with affiliations: Kassem M., German International University, Department of Robotics Engineering, New Administrative Capital, Egypt; Tolba K., German International University, Department of Robotics Engineering, New Administrative Capital, Egypt
Abstract: This paper presents a digital twin-based framework for geometric error modeling and inverse kinematics compensation in 5 -axis CNC machining. The proposed approach models ten geometric error sources using homogeneous transformation matrices embedded within a multibody representation of the machine kinematic chain. A complete digital twin is developed in Simulink from a CAD-derived model of an XYZAB machine and is used to analyze the propagation of individual and combined errors. An inverse kinematics formulation is introduced to address non-orthogonal rotary axes, where conventional Euler-based extraction becomes invalid under realistic machine deviations. A calibration method based on indirect point measurements is implemented within the digital twin to estimate geometric error parameters through a nonlinear system of equations, with simulated noise to replicate realistic measurement uncertainty. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework for identifying and compensating geometric deviations, enabling accurate axis command generation without hardware modification. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Simulation-Driven Cognitive Digital Twin MPC for Nonlinear Industrial Process Control

Authors with affiliations: Ansari M.A.T., Yokogawa, Dhahran, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Nonlinear industrial processes pose major challenges to conventional model predictive control (MPC) due to uncertainty, disturbances, and model drift. While digital twin based MPC improves prediction accuracy through high fidelity virtual models, it lacks autonomous learning and resilience. To address the lack of autonomous learning and uncertainty aware MPC in literally existing DT-MPC, a novel Simulation-Driven Cognitive Digital Twin MPC framework is proposed. This paper proposes a cognitive digital twin based MPC (CDT-MPC) framework that extends the traditional digital twin by integrating ensemble learning and Bayesian optimization as a cognitive learning layer. An ensemble of heterogeneous predictive models captures nonlinear dynamics and quantifies uncertainty, which is incorporated into an uncertainty-aware MPC formulation. Bayesian optimization enables autonomous tuning of ensemble and MPC parameters in a simulation-driven manner. The performance of proposed CD-MPC model is validated by benchmarking against Conventional MPC and Digital twin MPC using the standard evaluation metrics namely, RMSE, Constraint Violation (%) and disturbance recovery time. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces tracking error by over 55%, limits constraint violations to below 1%, and achieves disturbance recovery within 12 s, outperforming conventional MPC and digital twin MPC. The results confirm the effectiveness of cognitive digital twins for resilient nonlinear industrial control. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The rapid digitalization of renewable energy systems has made digital twin technology a transformative approach for modeling, monitoring, and optimizing wind turbines. This chapter presents a framework for an AI- powered digital twin that integrates multi- physics modeling, machine learning, and real- time data synchronization. It develops detailed aerodynamic, mechanical, electrical, structural, and thermal models forming a hybrid simulation grounded in physics. Artificial intelligence methods, from machine learning to physics- informed neural networks, enhance fault detection, anomaly diagnosis, and life prediction. A small- scale turbine simulation validates the framework, showing real- time operation, improved torque prediction, and precise anomaly detection. The discussion highlights future directions in multi- agent wind farm twins, uncertainty quantification, explainable AI, and self- evolving models, outlining a roadmap toward autonomous and trustworthy digital energy ecosystems. © 2026 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. Title: A fuzzy–digital twin optimization framework for simultaneous management of waste and energy consumption in sustainable manufacturing

Authors with affiliations: Nozari H., Department of Management, Azad University United Arab Emirates, Dubai, United Arab Emirates; Yordanova Z., Industrial Business Department, Business Faculty, University of National and World Economy, Sofia, Bulgaria
Abstract: Sustainable manufacturing systems require intelligent methods to balance economic performance with environmental responsibility. This research presents a digital twin-fuzzy multi-objective optimization framework for simultaneously managing cost, energy consumption, and waste in sustainable manufacturing. In this framework, fuzzy logic is used to model data uncertainty, a digital twin is used to obtain real-time data from the manufacturing process, and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is used to generate a Pareto front and analyze the relationships between economic and environmental objectives. The proposed model was tested in 10 simulated scenarios based on digital twin data. The results showed that the proposed framework maintained the service level above 95%, reduced the total cost by 14% and the amount of waste by 18% compared to the baseline. Pareto front analysis also showed that although there is a relative conflict between economic and environmental objectives, this conflict is controllable. Also, sensitivity analysis revealed that energy ceiling and machinery efficiency have the greatest impact on the sustainability and profitability of the system. Overall, the proposed framework provides a reliable, quantitative decision-making tool for managers and policymakers on the path to green and sustainable production. © (2026), (Ramazan YAMAN). Abstract: Underground Utility Digital Twins (UUDTs) are increasingly recognized as critical components of Urban Digital Twins (UDTs), yet their development remains constrained by fragmented records, incomplete geometry, semantic inconsistencies, and governance barriers. Unlike above ground assets, underground infrastructures are characterized by sparse observations, missing depth information, heterogeneous data ownership, and high safety implications, making reliable digital representation particularly challenging. Existing standards and sensing technologies improve data quality and detection, yet they do not provide mechanisms for reconstructing or inferring undocumented assets and missing geometric attributes. This paper presents a comprehensive review and conceptual synthesis of how Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) can address these structural limitations and provide a promising foundation for advancing the development and maintenance of UUDTs. We first review the core data, geometric, semantic, and governance challenges that undermine current Urban Digital Twin (UDT) implementations. We then systematically map major generative paradigms, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), diffusion models, transformer-based architectures, and multimodal generative frameworks, to specific underground modeling tasks such as sensor data synthesis, geometry and topology completion, semantic enrichment, multi-source data fusion, and uncertainty quantification. Building on this synthesis, we propose a task-oriented integration framework for embedding generative modules within urban digital twin workflows, with the aim of supporting probabilistic reconstruction, continuous updating, and risk-Aware decision support. By reframing underground infrastructure modeling as a probabilistic inference problem rather than a deterministic data integration exercise, this review establishes a conceptual foundation and research roadmap for next-generation UUDTs that are adaptive, uncertainty-Aware, and aligned with the safety and resilience requirements of smart cities.  © 2013 IEEE.

Abstract: This paper presents the first probabilistic Digital Twin of operational en route airspace, developed for the London Area Control Centre. The Digital Twin is intended to support the development and rigorous human-in-the-loop evaluation of AI agents for Air Traffic Control (ATC), providing a virtual representation of real-world airspace that enables safe exploration of higher levels of ATC automation. This paper makes three significant contributions: firstly, we demonstrate how historical and live operational data may be combined with a probabilistic, physics-informed machine learning model of aircraft performance to reproduce real-world traffic scenarios, while accurately reflecting the level of uncertainty inherent in ATC. Secondly, we develop a structured assurance case, following the Trustworthy and Ethical Assurance framework, to provide quantitative evidence for the Digital Twin’s accuracy and fidelity. This is crucial to building trust in this novel technology within this safety-critical domain. Thirdly, we describe how the Digital Twin forms a unified environment for agent testing and evaluation. This includes fast-time execution (up to x200 real-time), a standardised Python-based “gym” interface that supports a range of AI agent designs, and a suite of quantitative metrics for assessing performance. Crucially, the framework facilitates competency-based assessment of AI agents by qualified Air Traffic Control Officers through a Human Machine Interface. We also outline further applications and future extensions of the Digital Twin architecture. © 2026, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Inc, AIAA. All rights reserved.

Abstract: Digital Twin simulations have become a groundbreaking method in macroeconomic policy testing, as they allow simulating the complex economic systems in real-time and basing them on data. In this paper, the authors suggest an integrated Digital Twin framework, which involves the use of national accounts, financial measurements, and behavioral data and analytical methods, such as Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE), agent-based models, and hybrid artificial intelligence algorithms. The model enables a consistent alignment of the actual economic situation in the real world with the virtual one, thus enabling the policymakers to model various economic situations with a high degree of precision. The mathematical modeling layer represents nonlinear interactions among macroeconomic variables like GDP, inflation, employment and interest rates and involves constraints and conditions of equilibrium. Systematic modelling of policy shocks such as fiscal stimulus, monetary policy and external shocks are aimed at assessing the dynamic effects of these shocks. The simulation approach focuses on the design with scenario-based design, counterfactual experiment, and sensitivity analysis with robustness that takes into account the uncertainty and variability in the economic environment. The findings show that the suggested Digital Twin solution has a significant impact of enhancing the accuracy of the forecasts, a shorter time to evaluate the policy, and the efficiency of the decision-making process in comparison to the conventional econometric models.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Determinants of digital twin adoption readiness in logistics: Evidence from Egypt’s emerging logistics sector
Source title: Journal of Transport and Supply Chain Management
Affiliations: College of Business, Effat University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
Authors with affiliations: El-Nakib I., College of Business, Effat University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia; Elzarka S., College of Business, Effat University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Background: Digital twin technology can improve operational visibility, system monitoring and decision support in logistics. However, empirical evidence on organisational readiness for adoption remains limited in emerging logistics economies. Objectives: This study examines organisational readiness for digital twin adoption in Egypt’s logistics sector by assessing the effects of perceived operational benefits, digital workforce skills, managerial support and investment uncertainty. Method: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 500 logistics professionals across major logistics hubs in Egypt. The questionnaire measured perceived digital twin benefits, workforce digital capabilities, managerial commitment and financial uncertainty. Multiple regression analysis was used to test the determinants of adoption readiness. Results: Perceived operational benefits, digital workforce skills and managerial support had significant positive effects on adoption readiness. Investment uncertainty had a significant negative effect, showing that financial concerns remain an important implementation barrier. Conclusion: Digital twin adoption readiness in logistics depends less on technological feasibility alone and more on organisational capability, managerial commitment and investment clarity. Contribution: The study provides Egypt-specific evidence on the readiness conditions shaping digital twin adoption before full implementation. It offers practical guidance for logistics firms and policymakers seeking to move from digital twin awareness to adoption readiness. © 2026. The Authors.

Abstract: The Horizon Europe Project, ReNEW, uses the digital twin concept to simulate and model the complexity and interdependencies of the Inland Waterway Transport (IWT) system. This concept is used to design novel strategies to ensure network functionality despite climate change impacts on IWT. A digital twin is an accurate copy of a real object/item/system with associated characteristics in the digital world. Digital twin models can be developed using physics or statistics or combining the two. They can be used for simulation, classification, prediction, optimization, and more. This work proposes probabilistic digital twin modelling of complex IWT networks using Bayesian networks. Bayesian networks are statistical models that can address the complexity and uncertainty of the physical world. The availability of new data/information facilitates model updates, resulting in more accurate estimates. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: Digital twins are widely used in smart information systems to support monitoring and decisionmaking for complex infrastructure objects. However, in damaged infrastructure scenarios, automated digital twin updates often become unreliable due to incomplete, noisy, or contradictory data. This paper proposes a human-in-the-loop verification approach for infrastructure digital twins based on multimodal neural analysis and explicit uncertainty estimation. The method integrates visual, sensor, and textual data using modality-specific neural encoders and a multimodal fusion mechanism to estimate the object state. Prediction uncertainty is quantified using stochastic inference based on Monte Carlo Dropout and is used as a control signal for adaptive expert involvement. Human verification is triggered selectively only in cases associated with elevated uncertainty or potentially critical states, enabling a balance between automation and reliability. The proposed framework includes a formal problem formulation, a modular neural architecture, and a scalable verification workflow, demonstrating its applicability to real-world infrastructure monitoring under degraded data conditions.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The escalating climate and biodiversity crises present unprecedented decision-making challenges due to their complex, interconnected effects across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Current scientific approaches are fragmented and fail to capture the systemic cascading and compound risks that threaten both natural ecosystems and human societies. Current Digital Twin and Decision Support Systems lack the integrated multi-dimensional (spatial, temporal, climate, and biodiversity) modeling capability needed to capture the complex atmosphere-land-sea interactions and provide holistic, policy-ready decision intelligence for managing interconnected climate-biodiversity risks at ecosystem scale. TerraTwin introduces a holistic seven-dimensional (7D) Digital Twin of Ecosystem (DTE) that integrates the 3D spatial dimensions plus time, ecological, socioeconomic and decisional factors, thus advancing Decision Intelligence. The DTE representation is sustained by multiparametric marine, terrestrial and atmospheric environmental and biological data through advanced AI/ML analytics, physics-restricted modelling, and blockchain-secured harmonisation strategies. The proposed unified 7D DTE framework provides transparent, AI-augmented decision-making capabilities across multiple stakeholder domains, coupled with explainable policy recommendations for complex climate-biodiversity trade-offs under uncertainty. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Recent technological advances have expanded the availability of high-throughput biological datasets, opening the way to the reliable design of digital twins of biomedical systems or patients. Such computational tools represent key chemical reaction networks driving perturbation or drug response and can profoundly guide drug discovery and personalized therapeutics. Yet, their development still depends on laborious data integration by the human modeler, so that automated approaches are critically needed. The successes of data-driven system discovery in Physics, rooted in clean datasets and well-defined governing laws, have fueled interest in applying similar techniques in Biology, which presents unique challenges. Here, we reviewed 177 methodologies for automatically inferring digital twins from biological time series, which mostly involved symbolic or sparse regression, and recapitulated them in a Shiny app. We evaluated algorithms according to eight biological and methodological challenges, associated with integrating noisy/incomplete data, multiple conditions, prior knowledge, latent variables, or dealing with high dimensionality, unobserved variable derivatives, candidate library design, and uncertainty quantification. Upon these criteria, sparse regression generally outperformed symbolic regression, particularly when using Bayesian frameworks. Next, deep learning and large language models further emerge as innovative tools to integrate prior knowledge, although their reliability and consistency need to be improved. While no single method addresses all challenges, we argue that progress in learning digital twins will come from hybrid and modular frameworks combining chemical reaction network-based mechanistic grounding, Bayesian uncertainty quantification, and the generative and knowledge integration capacities of deep learning. To support their development, we further highlight key components required for future benchmark development to evaluate methods across all challenges. © The Author(s) 2026. Title: Digital twin-driven hybrid fuzzy Bayesian simulation framework for dynamic green credit risk assessment in manufacturing enterprises
Source title: International Journal of Modeling, Simulation, and Scientific Computing
Affiliations: Hunan International Economics University, Business School, Changsha, Hunan, 410205, China
Authors with affiliations: Yang N., Hunan International Economics University, Business School, Changsha, Hunan, 410205, China
Abstract: Green credit risk assessment for manufacturing enterprises is a dynamic and complex problem affected by operational states, environmental uncertainty, financial conditions, information quality, and interactive risk evolution. Traditional assessment methods depend heavily on low-frequency financial and disclosure data and therefore have limited ability to capture early risk signals arising from production operations, energy consumption, environmental performance, and supply-chain disturbances. In addition, conventional machine-learning models provide limited interpretability for causal dependence and uncertain risk propagation. This paper proposes a digital twin-driven hybrid fuzzy dynamic Bayesian network (DT-FDBN) framework for dynamic green credit risk assessment and scenario simulation in manufacturing enterprises. The framework integrates multi-source information covering financial solvency, production and equipment operation, energy consumption and emissions, green transition, environmental disclosure and information credibility, and the external environment into a unified enterprise digital-twin representation. Fuzzy evidence transformation is used to represent incomplete and imprecise observations, while credibility correction and group-level sensor reliability reduce the influence of unreliable digital-twin evidence. The DT-FDBN further models hierarchical risk dependence, temporal evolution, and probabilistic uncertainty propagation, supporting dynamic inference, key-factor diagnosis, multi-period prediction, and intervention-scenario simulation. Based on a semi-synthetic dataset containing 2160 enterprise-month observations from 60 manufacturing enterprises, the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.881, recall of 0.893, (Formula presented)-score of 0.869, AUC of 0.943, and Brier score of 0.079. It outperforms XGBoost and conventional fuzzy dynamic Bayesian networks in overall predictive and calibration performance and identifies operational and environmental deterioration earlier than financial-only assessment. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and dynamically adaptive modeling paradigm for manufacturing green credit risk management. © The Author(s) 2026

Abstract: Modern logistics systems, integral to global supply chains, face growing complexity and vulnerability to disruptions such as equipment failures, delivery delays, and demand fluctuations. To combat these challenges, digital twins have emerged as essential tools for real-time risk management. This paper explores the role of digital twins in logistics risk management, focusing on operational risk assessment and the application of the Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process method. By leveraging fuzzy logic, Fuzzy AHP enables the prioritization of key digital twin parameters, incorporating expert judgment and uncertainty. The study highlights the benefits of combining digital twins with Fuzzy AHP to improve risk identification, evaluation, and mitigation strategies in dynamic logistics environments. © European Alliance for Innovation 2026.

Title: Designing a Local Digital Twin for Port-City Energy Systems: Coupling Urban Building Energy Modeling with a Lightweight Onshore Power Supply Port Module and Urban Electrification Hooks
Source title: International Conference on the European Energy Market, EEM

Lyngby, Denmark
Abstract: Ports are electrifying through onshore power supply (OPS) while adjacent urban districts electrify heat and mobility, creating coupled peak-demand risks at shared distributiongrid boundaries. Yet port and city energy systems are often assessed in silos, limiting the ability to quantify coincident peaks, grid headroom, and the value of coordinated flexibility. This paper presents a Digital Twin-ready, decision-oriented coupling workflow that links an Urban Building Energy Model (UBEM) with a lightweight port energy module focused on OPS through a data-minimal coupling contract and an explicit orchestration layer. The contribution is framed as an early-stage screening architecture, rather than a fully operational Digital Twin, for translating simultaneous port-city electrification into feasibility indicators under shared local grid constraints. Uncertainty hooks (OPS uptake, electric vehicle (EV) / heat pump (HP) overlays, and assumed headroom) enable scenario stress-testing without changing the core modules. An executable illustrative workflow using a district UBEM profile and a synthetic OPS generator produces feasibility-driven planning outputs, including congestion exposure, OPS energy served versus reduced under peak management, and an OPS supportability frontier across headroom caps.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Digital Twin-Driven Substation Waterlogging Prediction Using Causal Inference and Deep Learning

Abstract: The increasing frequency of extreme weather events poses a significant threat to the resilience of power systems, with substation waterlogging emerging as a critical operational risk. Existing predictive models often struggle with the complexity and uncertainty of waterlogging phenomena, limited by their reliance on single-domain physical models and an inability to effectively fuse multi-source data or uncover the intricate causal relationships among contributing factors. This paper introduces a novel predictive framework driven by an intelligent agent, which integrates Digital Twin (DT) technology, causal inference, and deep learning to overcome these limitations. The framework leverages a high-fidelity digital twin to create a dynamic virtual representation of the substation, enabling real-time simulation and monitoring. Causal inference, implemented through a Bayesian Network (BN), is employed to discover and quantify the probabilistic dependencies among meteorological, hydrological, and infrastructural variables. A Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) model then utilizes these insights to deliver highly accurate, multi-horizon waterlogging predictions. The proposed framework demonstrates significant improvements in predictive accuracy and interpretability, providing a robust and proactive solution for substation disaster mitigation and enhancing the resilience of power grid infrastructure. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A structural response prediction of multi-linked floating offshore structures for digital twin implementation using Krylov subspace-based model order reduction
Source title: International Journal of Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering
Affiliations: Department of Ship & Ocean Engineering, Korea Research Institute of Ships & Ocean Engineering School, University of Science & Technology, Daejeon, South Korea; Eco-friendly Ocean Development Research Division, Korea Research Institute of Ships & Ocean Engineering, Daejeon, South Korea
Authors with affiliations: Sim K., Department of Ship & Ocean Engineering, Korea Research Institute of Ships & Ocean Engineering School, University of Science & Technology, Daejeon, South Korea; Lee K., Department of Ship & Ocean Engineering, Korea Research Institute of Ships & Ocean Engineering School, University of Science & Technology, Daejeon, South Korea, Eco-friendly Ocean Development Research Division, Korea Research Institute of Ships & Ocean Engineering, Daejeon, South Korea
Abstract: Offshore structures are generally designed based on conservative safety factors and operated. However, due to the uncertainty of ocean environment in actual operations, ensuring structural safety is challenging. In particular, unexpected extreme wave loads, structural degradation, and operational accidents can lead to structural damage, making it essential to implement digital twin technology capable of real-time structural health monitoring and prediction. In this study, a digital twin model for predicting the structural responses of floating offshore unit structures was developed using the Krylov subspace-based model order reduction method. The system matrix and regular wave load vectors for each frequency component were constructed based on fluid-structure coupled analysis. And snapshot wave load vectors were generated by superposing frequency components, which were then projected onto the Krylov subspace along with the system matrix to build a reduced order model. And the irregular wave loads from measured wave elevation were constructed by estimating the frequency components through spectral analysis. These reconstructed wave loads were subsequently applied to simulate the structural responses using the reduced order model. The prediction accuracy of reduced order model was evaluated by comparing predicted results with numerical simulations and measured data through model test. As a result, the reduced order model achieved approximately 99% prediction accuracy using over 10 degrees of freedom compared to the full order model, while also offering hundreds times faster simulation speed. In addition, comparison with model test showed that the prediction accuracy improved as more frequency components were used to construct the wave loads, achieving a maximum accuracy of 96.7%. © 2026 The Society of Naval Architects of Korea

Abstract: The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and flexible loads introduces variability and uncertainty into microgrids, complicating real-Time monitoring and control. Digital Twin (DT) technology a virtual replica synchronized with operational data offers an effective way to address these challenges. This paper presents a data-driven, hardware-independent DT framework for PV generation and flexible-load operation, validated via dataset replay of historical inverter data from Jubail Industrial City, Saudi Arabia. Three DT models were developed and compared: A machine-learning Random Forest (RF), an autoregressive with exogenous inputs (ARX) model, and a hybrid A R X+\mathbfR F residual-correction model. The RF achieved the highest accuracy (R2=0.988), the ARX provided interpretability with lower accuracy (R2=0.912), and the hybrid balanced both (R2=0.923). The DT was integrated with the ThingSpeak IoT cloud, where voltage and current were streamed as inputs, predicted power was computed online, and a control signal was generated for a flexible load. When the predicted PV power exceeds approximately 3 kW, the digital twin (DT) identifies surplus renewable energy and increases the lamp brightness to indicate higher flexible-load activity. Any remaining surplus is routed to battery energy storage systems (BESS), green-hydrogen electrolysers, and electric-vehicle (EV) chargers according to priority. When PV generation falls below 3 kW, the intensity of light decreases This intensity control maximizes renewable utilization, maintains balanced operation within the system framework. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and agent-based approaches to support intelligent and autonomous urban systems. However, existing reviews largely examine DTs, AI techniques, or agent-based approaches separately, leaving limited insight into how these dimensions interact and how such systems progress toward higher levels of intelligence and real-world deployment. This systematic literature review (SLR) analyzes 82 primary research studies describing AI-driven agent-based approaches in urban digital twins as a system of systems and found in four major scientific databases, i.e. IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library. The selected studies were systematically examined with respect to digital twin types, AI techniques used, agent type, agent roles, maturity level, application domains, and key challenges. As a result, we categorize digital twins into five types: conceptual DT, descriptive DT, predictive DT, prescriptive DT and autonomous DT, with the most frequent being the predictive DT. Reinforcement learning emerged as the most common AI technique, while the hierarchical agent taxonomy shows that multi-agent systems dominate at the architectural level, and decision-making and acting is the main role of agents, followed by control. We also identified that most studies remain at relatively low Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and rely predominantly on simulation-based or conceptual validation, revealing a substantial gap between technological advancement and real-world deployment. The analysis further shows that implementation challenges evolve across the DT life-cycle. Moreover, we found that only a limited proportion of studies explicitly address uncertainty, while the majority rely on deterministic or idealized assumptions. Our analysis further revealed that most urban digital twin systems are in the early stages of development, and we identified key research gaps and, based on this, suggested future research directions. Overall, this SLR provides a structured synthesis of AI-driven agent-based urban digital twins and identifies priorities for interoperability, standardized evaluation, real-world validation, and scalable autonomous urban systems.  © 2013 IEEE.

Abstract: Digital twins integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) are emerging as key enablers for realizing net-zero energy systems. AI-enhanced digital twins improve the intelligence, efficiency, resilience, and sustainability of energy infrastructures through continuous monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent control of modern power systems. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in AI-based digital twin applications in the energy domain, focusing on system architectures, enabling AI methodologies, practical deployments, and cybersecurity challenges. Core AI techniques, including machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, physics-informed models, and generative AI, are analyzed for grid optimization, predictive maintenance, renewable energy integration, and carbon-aware energy management. This paper examines security and trust issues through Zero-Trust architectures and governance frameworks for protecting critical energy infrastructures. Open research challenges such as scalability, data uncertainty, interoperability, model interpretability, and regulatory compliance are discussed to highlight existing research gaps. These insights guide future research and practical deployment of intelligent energy twins. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) enables noninvasive respiratory monitoring using commodity wireless devices, but deployment is hindered by domain shift across environments, hardware setups, and users. We propose TrustTwinCSI, a trust-aware digital twin framework that combines cross-domain training, uncertainty-aware inference, and volunteer-level personalization for CSI-based respiratory state recognition. A shared CNN+Transformer base model is trained on source domains, Monte Carlo dropout provides predictive uncertainty, and a trust gate supports selective prediction (accept vs. defer) and uncertainty-gated routing to volunteer-specific digital twins. Digital twins are adapted using a few-shot support set via head-only fine-tuning with L2-SP regularization and are accepted only if they improve on a disjoint calibration set, reducing negative transfer. On the ResMon dataset, the selected base model achieves mean Macro-F1 of about 0.77 across four unseen target domains. Selective prediction at τ = 0.80 improves Macro-F1 by +0.051 on accepted samples at 67.8% coverage, while trust-gated digital twin routing improves full-coverage Macro-F1 by +0.037 with 6.3 seconds average adaptation time per volunteer. These results show that uncertainty can be operationalized to improve reliability and regulate safe personalization under domain shift. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Robust Field-Focused Digital Twin for Real-Time Water-Quality Estimation and Alerting

Abstract: Sensors and communications should be model-driven in the digital twin that itself accurately represents control logic, so the treatment plant has accurate sanitation evaluations for assimilation decisions (and alarm notifications) even store-and-forward hours later. This work presents a high-fidelity and hardware-realistic digital twin framework to model probe physics, temperature-dependent conductance, reference-electrode drift, telemetry loss, fouling, biofilm-growth mechanism, and the maintenance cycles in order to quantify estimator and alarm performance under normal operational stressors. The twin closes a research gap by integrating a parametric state-space model with a hybrid assimilation toolchain: lightweight Kalman updates for near-real-time denoising, Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoothing for retrospective optimization, and robust residual screening for outlier rejection/gap filling. An alert engine uses standards-aligned thresholds, hysteresis, and time-over-threshold (TOT) rules (with continuous monitoring of residuals using Cumulative SUM [CUSUM] statistics at individual sensor nodes), as well as residual-driven CUSUM and Bayesian online change-point detection to trade off early warning versus nuisance reduction. Results for semisynthetic scenarios calibrated to reservoir, treatment plant, and wellfield conditions are presented, showing reductions of 48.6% in RMSE for pH and 42.3% for TDS; a decrease of the false alarm rate from 12.4% to 3.1%; and a mean reduction of detection delay as high as 38%. The platform consists of a reusable field-focused testbed for algorithm selection, calibration planning, operational SLO development, and operator training guidance. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The increasing deployment of renewable energy projects, particularly wind power, introduces significant operational uncertainty into modern power systems. Transmission System Operators (TSOs) rely on accurate short-term power forecasting to ensure grid stability and maintain economical system operation. However, the development and validation of deep learning-based forecasting models are often constrained by limited, noisy, or incomplete SCADA datasets, making it difficult to distinguish between data-quality issues and intrinsic algorithmic limitations. To overcome this challenge, we introduce an open-source, physics-informed digital twin framework for the pre-deployment validation of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. We developed a Python-based simulation engine that replicates the non-linear dynamics of a 2.3 MW wind turbine. The model strictly follows aerodynamic power conversion limits while capturing realistic atmospheric autocorrelation using Random Walk processes. Experimental sensitivity analysis confirms that standard LSTM architectures fail to identify patterns in uncorrelated stochastic noise, resulting in a Normalized Root Mean Square Error (nRMSE) exceeding 27%. Conversely, the proposed architecture with temporal feature embedding obtained an nRMSE of 2.25% on physically consistent synthetic data. This paper establishes the open-source Digital Twin as an essential verification layer to de-risk AI integration in national energy management systems prior to deployment.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Overspeed burst is a critical failure mode of discs, for which experimental validation is costly and destructive, while conventional finite element analysis (FEA) is computationally expensive and often inaccurate. To address these challenges, this study proposes a digital twin-based method for disc burst speed prediction by integrating multi-source uncertainty modelling, surrogate-based prediction, and adaptive model correction. A fracture strain criterion combined with FEA is used to estimate critical burst speeds, and a high-precision Kriging model is constructed via sequential sampling to improve prediction efficiency. Experimental data are incorporated to enable online correction of geometry and model parameters. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method improves prediction accuracy by 16.99% compared with conventional FEA, with the relative error of the actual burst speed reduced to 3.26%, while the computational time is reduced by approximately two orders of magnitude. The developed digital twin framework further supports the real-time updating of strain fields and the dynamic visualisation of the disc burst process. This method provides an accurate and efficient solution for disc burst prediction, supporting disc safety design and reliability assessment. © 2026 The Author(s).
