Title: Integrating Digital Twin technology in Quality 5.0 and operational excellence: a Fuzzy COPRAS and Monte Carlo uncertainty simulation approach
Source title: Digital Twin
Affiliations: International Business Management, International School of Management (ISM), Paris, France
Authors with affiliations: Bagherian A., International Business Management, International School of Management (ISM), Paris, France
Abstract: Existing literature on the topic of Digital Twin (DT) integration in Quality 5.0 predominantly focuses on technical performance indicators, including predictive maintenance and efficiency in the process, and ignores the essential real requirement of alignment with human-centric values, the necessity of sustainability, and the interdependencies of factors of implementation success. This study compares the integration of Digital Twin (DT) in Quality 5.0, which is based on human-centric and sustainability-driven operational excellence. It allocates implementation criteria and alternatives in priority using a three-level Fuzzy COPRAS model with Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification and Sobel sensitivity analysis. A participation of 74 experts and a case study on the automotive industry reveal that Sustainability in Quality Improvement (SQI) is the best driver of improvement, in addition to conventional efficiency. Major sub-criteria are MES/ERP integration (MEI) and risk management (RM-DTQ) as well as root cause analysis (RCAE). IoT (Internet of Things)-based applications, in particular, continuous improvement, were the highest ranked. Composite sensitivity was high in hybrid (AI+IoT) strategies (0.991). Validation of cases showed a reduction of 25% defects and 18 percent energy saving. The research offers a statistically proven decision model to match the adoption of DT with sustainability, IoT-based enhancement, risk management, and human collaboration. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: ezTwin: A Scalable Framework for Rapid Building Digital Twin for Hydro-Informatics
Source title: World Environmental and Water Resources Congress 2026: Krewe of Innovation - Proceedings of World Environmental and Water Resources Congress 2026
Affiliations: Dept. of Computer Science, Univ. of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL, United States; CIROH, Univ. of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL, United States
Authors with affiliations: Arefin M., Dept. of Computer Science, Univ. of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL, United States; Feng X., CIROH, Univ. of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL, United States; He H., Dept. of Computer Science, Univ. of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL, United States
Abstract: Hydrologic digital twins have transformed water-level monitoring by integrating real-time data with predictive modeling, yet the rapid deployment of location-specific systems remains challenging. To address these challenges, the ezTwin framework was introduced, which can create hydrologic digital twins anywhere on Earth using minimal geospatial inputs. Using reservoir coordinates and a curvilinear river centerline, ezTwin creates geo-registered 3D scenes in Unreal Engine with Cesium-based Google 3D Tiles. It also programmatically places channel-aligned anchor points, which render live water levels and variations in river bathymetry that change with distance along the channel. To accelerate in situ data simulation and calibration, ezTwin integrates an unmanned surface vessel robot to transmit river depth data from sonar to the twin for real-time mesh refinement. The twin can pre-plan “virtual transects” to simulate sensor returns and dispatch these routes to the robot. It dynamically redirects the vessel to areas with high uncertainty, ensuring alignment between simulated and actual conditions. ezTwin simplifies deployment, enables flood scenario planning, and maintains real-time synchronization with physical conditions, improving decision-making. © ASCE.

Abstract: Autonomous vehicles must make reliable safety decisions despite perception noise and tight timing constraints. This work presents a Vehicle Digital Twin (VDT) architecture that incorporates a formally verified hybrid automaton as its supervisory controller. The automaton specifies discrete safety modes, continuous timing variables, and perception-driven transitions, and is verified offline using SMT-based LTL model checking to ensure determinism, freedom from deadlock, and bounded reaction time. At runtime, buffered perception inputs and staleness checks are used to trigger only those transitions consistent with the verified model, maintaining robustness to noisy or transient detections. We instantiate the approach for pedestrian-protection and evaluate it on standardized Euro NCAP scenarios within CARLA. The system consistently produces stable and interpretable braking decisions and maintains reaction times within the verified bounds, including under perception uncertainty. These results indicate that integrating a verified hybrid automaton directly into the VDT's operational loop is a practical route toward runtime-assured safety supervision in perception-driven vehicle systems.  © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Digital Twins Engineering: Workflow Patterns, Gaps, and Research Opportunities
Source title: Advances in Information, Electronic and Electrical Engineering, AIEEE 2026 - Proceedings of the 13th IEEE Workshop
Affiliations: Institute of Information Technology, Riga Technical University, Riga, Latvia
Authors with affiliations: Korcevskis M., Institute of Information Technology, Riga Technical University, Riga, Latvia; Pecerska J., Institute of Information Technology, Riga Technical University, Riga, Latvia
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into Digital Twin systems to enhance monitoring, prediction, optimization, and decision-making across industrial and infrastructure domains. However, existing research often reports AI-enabled Digital Twins within isolated application contexts, resulting in limited conceptual clarity regarding how AI methods align with the overall Digital Twin engineering workflow. This paper provides a focused conceptual synthesis of recent representative publications and organizes AI integration using a workflow-oriented analytical lens. Four dominant integration patterns are identified: AI-enhanced state estimation, hybrid data-driven modelling, reinforcement learning-based optimization, and AI-supported decision orchestration. Across domains, recurring challenges include workflow fragmentation, validation of embedded AI components, uncertainty management, interoperability, economic justification, and cybersecurity concerns. The findings highlight the need for architecture-level integration, standardized validation approaches, and governance-Aware design principles to support robust and scalable AI-enabled Digital Twins.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Route and Wind Aware Digital Twin Framework for ADS-C based Aircraft Trajectory Prediction Communication Loss
Source title: 2026 International Conference on Electrical/Electronics, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, and Informatics, ICERAI 2026
Affiliations: Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States
Authors with affiliations: Baba S.M., Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States; Sreepathi B.K., Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States; Ganesan C., Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States; Mustaphi S., Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States; Alhabshi M., Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States; Arora K., Golden Gate University, San Francisco, United States
Abstract: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Contract (ADS-C) is the primary surveillance mechanism used by aircraft in oceans and remote regions where radar coverage is unavailable, and ADS-B coverage is limited. Although ADS-C reports are highly accurate, they are transmitted only at specific events, not continuously. As a result, extended communication gaps may occur due to satellite outages, avionics failures, and abnormal operational conditions. During such gaps, conventional trajectory prediction methods rapidly lose accuracy and implicitly assume that the aircraft could be located isotropic. This leads to extensive and operationally unrealistic search regions, complicating air traffic management and search-and-rescue (SAR) decision-making. This paper proposes a digital twin framework that integrates a numerically stable local East-North-Up(ENU) Kalman filtering architecture, soft geometric constraints derived from the flight management system route intent, and selective wind-aware state propagation during communication silence. Unlike baseline kinematic filters, the proposed framework explicitly decomposes uncertainty into along-track and cross-track components, enabling the construction of bounded, anisotropic uncertainty corridors rather than unconstrained circular regions. The framework is evaluated using a real dataset from aircraft experiencing a prolonged communication loss. Despite operating in prediction-only mode for most of the flight, the digital twin maintains the possible aircraft location within a small and well-defined area. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is practical and reliable, aligning with operational SAR reasoning observed in MH370-style investigations, and establishes a foundation for resilient oceanic surveillance under communication loss. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Physics-Embedded Hybrid Neural ODE With Digital Twin Residuals for Fault Diagnosis in Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems
Source title: IEEE Access
Affiliations: Sultan Qaboos University, College of Engineering, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Muscat, 123, Oman
Authors with affiliations: Mansouri M., Sultan Qaboos University, College of Engineering, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Muscat, 123, Oman
Abstract: Accurate and interpretable fault diagnosis in renewable energy systems remains challenging due to measurement noise, nonlinear operating conditions, model uncertainty, and the presence of interacting fault mechanisms. This paper proposes a Physics-Embedded Hybrid Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (PE-HANODE) framework augmented with Digital Twin (DT) residual information for robust diagnosis of multi-fault, non-Gaussian, and time-varying conditions in grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems. The main contribution of this work is not the introduction of individual new learning components, but the development of a unified diagnostic framework that integrates complementary physics-guided representations, lightweight Digital Twin residual reasoning, attention-guided feature weighting, and Neural ODE-based temporal modeling to address limitations of conventional data-driven PV fault diagnosis approaches. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components. First, physics-informed features derived from PV electrical characteristics and operating principles provide physically meaningful representations of system behavior rather than relying solely on data-driven feature extraction. Second, a lightweight DT model identified from healthy operating data generates residual signals that quantify deviations between expected nominal responses and measured system behavior, while the SDM is employed for physical consistency verification and parameter calibration rather than direct residual generation. Third, an attention-guided Neural ODE architecture exploits continuous latent-state evolution to capture temporal dependencies while prioritizing diagnostically relevant features. The DT residuals are fused with measured and physics-informed variables and incorporated into the Neural ODE learning process, enabling improved discrimination of subtle and overlapping fault signatures under noisy and incomplete sensing conditions. The attention mechanism provides feature-level interpretability by highlighting the relative importance of diagnostic variables and residual signals contributing to classification decisions, rather than performing direct physical root-cause identification. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated using both synthetic PV fault datasets for controlled proof-of-concept evaluation and experimental data obtained from an emulated laboratory-scale PV platform representing more realistic operating conditions. Additional robustness studies are conducted under Laplace and uniform noise perturbations to evaluate resilience against non-Gaussian measurement uncertainty. Comparative results demonstrate that the integration of physics-guided features, DT residual information, attention-based feature weighting, and continuous-time latent representation learning provides consistent diagnostic improvements compared with conventional machine learning and recurrent neural network baselines, including LSTM and GRU models. Ablation studies, statistical performance analysis, and computational complexity evaluations are further conducted to quantify the contribution of each framework component and assess the trade-off between diagnostic performance and computational requirements. Interpretability analyses based on attention-weight distributions and fault-confusion assessment provide insights into feature importance patterns within the learned diagnostic representation. The proposed PE-HANODE framework offers a physics-consistent and interpretable solution for intelligent fault diagnosis by unifying physics-informed feature construction, lightweight Digital Twin residual generation, and continuous-time deep learning within a single diagnostic architecture. The proposed framework demonstrates promising capability for real-time PV monitoring under evaluated laboratory conditions, while further utility-scale field validation remains necessary before large-scale industrial deployment.INDEX TERMS Physics-embedded neural ODE, digital twin, fault diagnosis, photovoltaic systems, attention mechanism, explainable artificial intelligence, continuous-time learning.  © 2013 IEEE.

Title: Autonomous Robotaxi Docking Using Digital Twin Vision and LiDAR Planning
Source title: 2026 International Conference on Green Technologies and Sustainable Solutions, GTSS 2026
Affiliations: OH, United States; MI, United States; CA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Sucharitha R.S., OH, United States; Sanikal V., MI, United States; Choudhary R., CA, United States; Pradhan S., MI, United States
Abstract: Autonomous robotaxi fleets need a reliable way to charge without human help. For this to work, the charging process must be fully automated. Robotic charging is more demanding than ordinary autonomous parking. The vehicle has to align precisely with a fixed charging interface. The system also depends on accurate perception, motion planning, and manipulator reachability. This study presents a digital-twin-based approach for automated charging. The setup uses both camera and LiDAR sensors. These sensors guide a robotic arm as it connects to the vehicle. The framework includes vehicle-motion planning, charging-port detection, and pose estimation that accounts for uncertainty. A digital twin of the charging station provides key information. It includes charger geometry, docking points, safety zones, and regions with higher uncertainty. The vehicle must reach a suitable docking position so the manipulator can operate within limited pose errors. This requirement defines a docking-constrained task. The system is tested in a CARLA simulation environment. The simulation includes dynamic agents and sensor noise. Results show that planning with docking semantics and uncertainty improves first-attempt connection success. It also reduces the need for late-stage replanning when compared with navigation-focused baselines. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Military Digital Twins - A Data-hardened Architecture for Digital Twins to Enable Operational Resilience in Adversarial Environments
Source title: Proceedings - International Conference on Air Defense and Security, ICADS 2026
Affiliations: ABB Corporate Research, Bangalore, India; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, NIST University, Berhampur, India
Authors with affiliations: Rath A., ABB Corporate Research, Bangalore, India; Patra M.R., Department of Computer Science and Engineering, NIST University, Berhampur, India
Abstract: We propose a data-hardened architecture for military digital twins that can enable resilient, integrated warfare under contested environments. We first elicit the foundational requirements of a military digital twin and use them to derive its defining architectural choices. Designed explicitly for adversarial environments, it adopts a zero-trust posture in every design decision and employs Bayesian consensus mechanisms to build trust dynamically over time, enabling battlefield assets to verify one another for signs of compromise. Furthermore, the architecture mitigates the challenges of intermittent, low-bandwidth connectivity at the edge by employing a hybrid construct: a lightweight, low-fidelity edge twin paired with a high-fidelity command-center twin. This division of labour enhances resilience, maintains operational continuity, and strengthens the overall robustness of the military digital twin ecosystem. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Validating Digital Twins with Tactile-Visual Liver Phantoms for Robot-Assisted Surgical Workflows
Source title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
Affiliations: Academic Informatics Office, National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore, Singapore
Authors with affiliations: Mao C., Academic Informatics Office, National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore, Singapore; Tan Y.Z., Academic Informatics Office, National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore, Singapore; Gao Y., Academic Informatics Office, National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore, Singapore
Abstract: This study presents a novel physical liver phantom that replicates the mechanical and visual properties of healthy, fatty, and fibrotic liver tissues to support verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification in digital twin frameworks for liver surgery. Simulating these three common liver conditions improves phantom fidelity for surgical training and model validation. We evaluated multiple materials (agar, gelatin, and konnyaku) for phantom fabrication and conducted a twelve-question survey with 25 surgeons to optimize formulations based on tactile realism and visual appearance. Standard surgical interactions (compression, pinching, pulling and cutting) were performed on both phantoms and fresh porcine liver models using the da Vinci® Xi surgical system. Stereo endoscopic video recordings enabled a comparative analysis of visual fidelity and tissue deformation under surgical manipulation. Mechanical properties (compressive and tensile Young’s modulus) were quantitatively measured under mechanical testing and compared with real tissue measurements in literature. The resulting phantom, validated through surgeon feedback and mechanical testing, provides a tangible platform for physical model validation and surgeon-in-the-loop simulations in digital twin applications. This work advances digital twin methodologies by offering a realistic testbed for model calibration and verification, bridging computational models and real surgical scenarios. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.
